THIS IS MY COMPLETE CLIENT SCRIPT
// ============================================================
// PTS3 Test - Client Script (Single-Lane Operator Mode)
// Spec: 12_LIVE_UPDATE_FLOW.md, 18_FINAL_DOCTYPE_SPEC_REVISED.md
//
// Single-lane operator console. Uses lane 1 only. Hides data-entry fields.
// PTS3 Result created only when connector calls save_final_result (on completion).
// ============================================================

(function () {
  /** F12 console: filter by [PTS3] */
  function pts3Dbg() {
    try {
      if (typeof console !== "undefined" && console.debug) {
        var a = Array.prototype.slice.call(arguments);
        console.debug.apply(console, ["[PTS3]"].concat(a));
      }
    } catch (e) {}
  }

  const REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS = 1750;
  const LANE_NO = 1;
  const PTS3_SIDEBAR_WIDTH = 180;  // Left sidebar width (px) when on PTS3 Test - edit to reduce/increase
  const PTS3_SIDEBAR_COLLAPSED = true;  // Set true to collapse sidebar when opening PTS3 Test

  // Keep last known sweep graph/table visible across Mode runs
  // (ERP live_* fields can be cleared/overwritten when a new action starts)
  const PTS3_UI_CACHE_KEY = "__pts3_ui_cache_v1";

  if (document.getElementById("pts3-client-style") == null) {
    const style = document.createElement("style");
    style.id = "pts3-client-style";
    style.textContent = ".pts3-dashboard{max-width:100%;width:100%;}.pts3-lane-box{border:1px solid #d1d8dd;border-radius:4px;padding:1rem;}.pts3-lane-title{margin:0;font-size:1.1rem;}.pts3-station{margin:0;font-size:0.85em;color:#6c7680;}.pts3-header-row{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;align-items:center;gap:0.5rem;margin-bottom:0.5rem;}.pts3-header-left{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;align-items:center;gap:0.5rem;min-width:0;flex:1 1 auto;}.pts3-header-right{margin-left:auto;display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;align-items:center;gap:0.5rem;justify-content:flex-end;}.pts3-header-left .pts3-serial-row{margin:0;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:0.5rem;}.pts3-header-left .pts3-serial-row input{width:180px;padding:4px 8px;}.pts3-header-left .pts3-actions{margin:0;display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:4px;}.pts3-header-left .pts3-actions .btn{margin:0;}.pts3-summary{margin:0.5rem 0;font-size:0.9em;color:#6c7680;}.pts3-summary-item{margin-right:1rem;}.pts3-error{color:#e74c3c;margin:0.5rem 0;}.pts3-progress{color:#3498db;margin:0.5rem 0;}.pts3-playing-freq{font-size:1.1em;color:#2980b9;}.pts3-no-data{color:#8d99a6;font-style:italic;}.pts3-lrd-table,.pts3-graph-table{font-size:0.85em;}.pts3-status-running{color:#3498db;}.pts3-status-requested,.pts3-status-queued{color:#f39c12;}.pts3-status-done{color:#27ae60;}.pts3-status-failed,.pts3-status-aborted{color:#e74c3c;}.pts3-lane-log{font-family:monospace;font-size:11px;background:#1e1e1e;color:#d4d4d4;padding:8px;border-radius:4px;max-height:200px;overflow-y:auto;white-space:pre-wrap;word-break:break-all;margin-top:0.5rem;}.pts3-charts-row{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:0.75rem;align-items:flex-start;width:100%;margin:0.25rem 0;}.pts3-chart-wrap{flex:1 1 48%;min-width:550px;margin:0;overflow-x:auto;}.pts3-chart-wrap svg.pts3-chart-svg{width:100%;height:auto;display:block;}";
    document.head.appendChild(style);
  }

  frappe.ui.form.on("PTS3 Test", {
    onload: function (frm) {
      ensure_lane1(frm);
      hide_operator_fields(frm);
      apply_full_width_form(frm);
    },
    refresh: function (frm) {
      ensure_lane1(frm);
      hide_operator_fields(frm);
      render_lane_dashboard(frm);
      start_auto_refresh_if_needed(frm);
    }
  });

  function hide_operator_fields(frm) {
    var hidden = ["naming_series", "name_serial_slug", "name_op_short", "test_status", "station_name", "operator", "remarks"];
    hidden.forEach(function (fn) {
      if (frm.fields_dict[fn]) {
        frm.set_df_property(fn, "hidden", 1);
      }
    });
    // target_pc must stay visible (or at least not hidden): hidden Data fields often reject
    // frm.set_value in the browser, so the Station box could not update the document.
    if (frm.fields_dict.target_pc) {
      frm.set_df_property("target_pc", "hidden", 0);
      frm.set_df_property("target_pc", "read_only", 0);
    }
    if (frm.fields_dict.lanes) {
      frm.set_df_property("lanes", "hidden", 1);
    }

  function ensure_lane1(frm) {
    var lanes = frm.doc.lanes || [];
    var has1 = lanes.some(function (r) { return parseInt(r.lane_no, 10) === LANE_NO; });
    if (!has1) {
      var row = frm.add_child("lanes");
      row.lane_no = LANE_NO;
      row.lane_action_status = "Idle";
      row.lane_action = "";
      row.pcb_serial_no = "";
      frm.refresh_field("lanes");
    }
  }

  function apply_full_width_form(frm) {
    frm.$wrapper.parents(".form-layout, .form-container, .layout-main, .page-content").addClass("pts3-full-width-form");
    document.body.classList.add("pts3-test-page");
    setTimeout(collapse_sidebar_for_pts3, 100);
    if (!window.__pts3_route_cleanup) {
      window.__pts3_route_cleanup = true;
      frappe.router.on("change", function () {
        var r = frappe.router.current_route || [];
        if (r[0] !== "Form" || r[1] !== "PTS3 Test") {
          $(".form-layout, .form-container, .layout-main, .page-content").removeClass("pts3-full-width-form");
          document.body.classList.remove("pts3-test-page");
        }
      });
    }
  }

  function collapse_sidebar_for_pts3() {
    try {
      if (frappe.desk && frappe.desk.sidebar && typeof frappe.desk.sidebar.collapse === "function") {
        frappe.desk.sidebar.collapse();
        return;
      }
      if (frappe.ui && frappe.ui.sidebar && typeof frappe.ui.sidebar.collapse === "function") {
        frappe.ui.sidebar.collapse();
        return;
      }
      var $toggle = $(".sidebar-toggle, .menu-btn, [data-toggle='sidebar'], .page-head .menu-btn, .navbar .toggle-sidebar").first();
      if ($toggle.length && !$("body").hasClass("sidebar-collapsed")) {
        $toggle.trigger("click");
      }
    } catch (e) {}
  }

  // -----------------------
  // 2. Button actions (server API only, internal codes)
  // -----------------------
  function request_lane_action(frm, lane_no, action) {
    if (!frm.doc.name) {
      frappe.msgprint(__("Save the document first."));
      return;
    }
    var serial = get_lane_field(frm, lane_no, "pcb_serial_no") || "";
    if (!serial.trim()) {
      frappe.msgprint(__("Enter PCB Serial No before requesting action."));
      return;
    }
    frappe.call({
      method: "pts3_api",
      args: {
        api_cmd: "request_lane_action",
        docname: frm.doc.name,
        lane_no: lane_no,
        action: action
      },
      callback: function (r) {
        pts3Dbg("request_lane_action response", r && r.message ? r.message : r);
        if (r && r.message && r.message.ok) {
          frm.reload_doc();
        } else if (r && r.message && r.message.reason) {
          frappe.msgprint(__("Request failed: {0}", [r.message.reason]));
        } else if (r && r.exc) {
          frappe.msgprint(__("Request failed: {0}", [r.exc]));
        }
      },
      error: function (r) {
        pts3Dbg("request_lane_action error", r);
      }
    });
  }

  function request_abort(frm, lane_no) {
    frappe.call({
      method: "pts3_api",
      args: {
        api_cmd: "request_abort",
        docname: frm.doc.name,
        lane_no: lane_no
      },
      callback: function (r) {
        pts3Dbg("request_abort response", r && r.message ? r.message : r);
        if (r && r.message && r.message.ok) {
          frm.reload_doc();
        }
      },
      error: function (r) {
        pts3Dbg("request_abort error", r);
      }
    });
  }

  function reset_lane(frm, lane_no) {
    frappe.call({
      method: "pts3_api",
      args: {
        api_cmd: "reset_lane",
        docname: frm.doc.name,
        lane_no: lane_no
      },
      callback: function (r) {
        pts3Dbg("reset_lane response", r && r.message ? r.message : r);
        if (r && r.message && r.message.ok) {
          frm.reload_doc();
        }
      },
      error: function (r) {
        pts3Dbg("reset_lane error", r);
      }
    });
  }

  function get_lane_row(frm, lane_no) {
    var lanes = frm.doc.lanes || [];
    return lanes.find(function (r) { return parseInt(r.lane_no, 10) === parseInt(lane_no, 10); }) || null;
  }

  function get_lane_field(frm, lane_no, field) {
    var row = get_lane_row(frm, lane_no);
    return row ? row[field] : "";
  }

  // -----------------------
  // 3. Auto-refresh loop + snapshot merge
  // -----------------------
  function is_active_status(s) {
    var lower = (s || "").toLowerCase();
    return lower === "requested" || lower === "queued" || lower === "running";
  }

  function start_auto_refresh_if_needed(frm) {
    if (frm.__pts3_refresh_timer) {
      clearInterval(frm.__pts3_refresh_timer);
      frm.__pts3_refresh_timer = null;
    }

    var lane1 = get_lane_row(frm, LANE_NO);
    var active = lane1 ? is_active_status(lane1.lane_action_status) : false;

    if (!active || !frm.doc.name) return;

    frm.__pts3_refresh_timer = setInterval(function () {
      frappe.call({
        method: "pts3_api",
        args: {
          api_cmd: "get_status_snapshot",
          docname: frm.doc.name
        },
        callback: function (r) {
          if (!r || !r.message || !r.message.ok) {
            pts3Dbg("get_status_snapshot not ok", r);
            return;
          }
          const data = r.message;
          const snapshot_lanes = data.lanes || [];
          var L1 = snapshot_lanes.find(function (x) { return parseInt(x.lane_no, 10) === LANE_NO; });
          if (L1) {
            pts3Dbg(
              "snapshot lane1 status=" + (L1.lane_action_status || "") +
                " latest_result_id=" + (L1.latest_result_id || "") +
                " live_graph_len=" + String(L1.live_graph_json || "").length +
                " live_table_len=" + String(L1.live_table_json || "").length
            );
          }

          merge_snapshot_into_form(frm, snapshot_lanes);
          render_lane_dashboard(frm);

          const stillActive = snapshot_lanes.some(function (L) {
            return is_active_status(L.lane_action_status);
          });
          if (!stillActive && frm.__pts3_refresh_timer) {
            clearInterval(frm.__pts3_refresh_timer);
            frm.__pts3_refresh_timer = null;
            pts3Dbg("auto-refresh stopped (lane no longer active)");
          }
        },
        error: function (r) {
          pts3Dbg("get_status_snapshot error", r);
        }
      });
    }, REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS);
  }

  function merge_snapshot_into_form(frm, snapshot_lanes) {
    if (!frm[PTS3_UI_CACHE_KEY]) frm[PTS3_UI_CACHE_KEY] = {};
    const cache = frm[PTS3_UI_CACHE_KEY];
    const lanes = frm.doc.lanes || [];
    snapshot_lanes.forEach(function (snap) {
      const ln = parseInt(snap.lane_no, 10);
      const row = lanes.find(function (r) {
        return parseInt(r.lane_no, 10) === ln;
      });
      if (row) {
        row.lane_action_status = snap.lane_action_status || row.lane_action_status;
        row.live_graph_json = snap.live_graph_json !== undefined ? snap.live_graph_json : row.live_graph_json;
        row.live_table_json = snap.live_table_json !== undefined ? snap.live_table_json : row.live_table_json;
        row.live_status = snap.live_status !== undefined ? snap.live_status : row.live_status;
        row.live_current_freq = snap.live_current_freq !== undefined ? snap.live_current_freq : row.live_current_freq;
        row.live_current_mode = snap.live_current_mode !== undefined ? snap.live_current_mode : row.live_current_mode;
        row.live_progress_message = snap.live_progress_message !== undefined ? snap.live_progress_message : row.live_progress_message;
        row.pass_fail = snap.pass_fail !== undefined ? snap.pass_fail : row.pass_fail;
        row.dominant_channel = snap.dominant_channel !== undefined ? snap.dominant_channel : row.dominant_channel;
        row.max_value = snap.max_value !== undefined ? snap.max_value : row.max_value;
        row.latest_result_id = snap.latest_result_id !== undefined ? snap.latest_result_id : row.latest_result_id;
        row.error_message = snap.error_message !== undefined ? snap.error_message : row.error_message;
        row.lane_log = snap.lane_log !== undefined ? snap.lane_log : row.lane_log;

        // Cache: only update when incoming value is non-empty
        if (!cache[ln]) cache[ln] = {};
        if (snap.live_graph_json) cache[ln].live_graph_json = snap.live_graph_json;
        if (snap.live_table_json) cache[ln].live_table_json = snap.live_table_json;
      }
    });
  }

  // -----------------------
  // 4. Dashboard HTML (single lane card)
  // -----------------------
  function render_lane_dashboard(frm) {
    var container = frm.fields_dict.lane_dashboard && frm.fields_dict.lane_dashboard.$wrapper;
    if (!container) return;

    var lane = get_lane_row(frm, LANE_NO);
    if (!lane) return;

    var status = lane.lane_action_status || "Idle";
    var serial = lane.pcb_serial_no || "";
    var isActive = is_active_status(status);
    var targetPc = frm.doc.target_pc || "";

    var html = '<div class="pts3-dashboard">';
    html += '<div class="pts3-lane-box" data-lane="' + LANE_NO + '">';
    html += '<div class="pts3-header-row">';
    html += '<div class="pts3-header-left">';
    html += '<div class="pts3-serial-row"><label>PCB Serial No:</label> ';
    html += '<input type="text" class="pts3-serial-input" data-lane="' + LANE_NO + '" value="' + escape_html(serial) + '" placeholder="Enter serial" />';
    html += '<button class="btn btn-sm btn-default pts3-btn-save-serial">Save</button></div>';

    html += '<div class="pts3-actions">';
    html += '<button class="btn btn-sm btn-primary pts3-btn-action" data-lane="' + LANE_NO + '" data-action="step_sweep">Step Sweep</button>';
    html += '<button class="btn btn-sm btn-default pts3-btn-action" data-lane="' + LANE_NO + '" data-action="mode1">Mode 1</button>';
    html += '<button class="btn btn-sm btn-default pts3-btn-action" data-lane="' + LANE_NO + '" data-action="mode2">Mode 2</button>';
    html += '<button class="btn btn-sm btn-default pts3-btn-action" data-lane="' + LANE_NO + '" data-action="mode3">Mode 3</button>';
    html += '<button class="btn btn-sm btn-default pts3-btn-action" data-lane="' + LANE_NO + '" data-action="mode0">Mode 0</button>';
    html += '<button class="btn btn-sm btn-default pts3-btn-action" data-lane="' + LANE_NO + '" data-action="full_test">Full Test</button>';
    if (isActive) {
      html += '<button class="btn btn-sm btn-danger pts3-btn-stop" data-lane="' + LANE_NO + '">Stop</button>';
    }
    html += '<button class="btn btn-sm btn-default pts3-btn-reset" data-lane="' + LANE_NO + '">Reset</button>';
    html += "</div>";
    html += '<div class="pts3-header-right">';
    html += '<h4 class="pts3-lane-title"><span class="pts3-status pts3-status-' + status.toLowerCase() + '">' + escape_html(status) + '</span></h4>';
    html += '<div class="pts3-station">Station: <input type="text" class="pts3-target-pc-input" value="' + escape_html(targetPc) + '" placeholder="e.g. PTS3-PC-01" style="width:140px;padding:2px 6px;" /></div>';
    html += "</div></div>";

    html += '<div class="pts3-summary">';
    html += '<span class="pts3-summary-item">Pass/Fail: ' + escape_html(lane.pass_fail || "-") + '</span> ';
    html += '<span class="pts3-summary-item">Dominant: ' + escape_html(lane.dominant_channel || "-") + '</span> ';
    html += '<span class="pts3-summary-item">Max: ' + (lane.max_value != null ? lane.max_value : "-") + '</span> ';
    if (lane.latest_result_id) {
      html += '<span class="pts3-summary-item"><a href="#Form/PTS3 Result/' + encodeURIComponent(lane.latest_result_id) + '" target="_blank">' + escape_html(lane.latest_result_id) + "</a></span>";
    }
    html += "</div>";

    if (lane.error_message) {
      html += '<div class="pts3-error">' + escape_html(lane.error_message) + "</div>";
    }

    if (isActive && (lane.live_progress_message || lane.live_current_freq != null)) {
      var playingText = lane.live_current_freq != null ? ("Playing: " + lane.live_current_freq + " Hz") : escape_html(lane.live_progress_message || "");
      html += '<div class="pts3-progress pts3-playing-freq"><strong>' + playingText + '</strong></div>';
    }

    html += '<div class="pts3-live-graph" data-lane="' + LANE_NO + '">';
    html += render_live_graph(lane, frm);
    html += "</div>";

    html += '<div class="pts3-live-table" data-lane="' + LANE_NO + '">';
    html += render_live_table(lane, frm);
    html += "</div>";

    var laneLog = (lane.lane_log || "").trim();
    if (laneLog || isActive) {
      html += '<div class="pts3-lane-log-wrap" style="margin-top:0.75rem;"><strong>Scope / Connector Log</strong>';
      html += '<div class="pts3-lane-log" data-lane="' + LANE_NO + '">' + escape_html(laneLog || "(waiting for output...)") + "</div></div>";
    }

    html += "</div></div>";
    container.html(html);

    container.find(".pts3-target-pc-input").on("change", function () {
      var val = $(this).val() || "";
      frm.set_value("target_pc", val);
      frm.dirty();
    });

    container.find(".pts3-serial-input").on("change", function () {
      var val = $(this).val() || "";
      var row = get_lane_row(frm, LANE_NO);
      if (row) {
        row.pcb_serial_no = val;
        frm.dirty();
      }
    });

    container.find(".pts3-btn-save-serial").on("click", function () {
      var serialVal = container.find(".pts3-serial-input").val() || "";
      var pcVal = container.find(".pts3-target-pc-input").val() || "";
      var row = get_lane_row(frm, LANE_NO);
      if (row) {
        row.pcb_serial_no = serialVal;
      }
      frm.set_value("target_pc", pcVal);
      frm.save();
    });

    container.find(".pts3-btn-action").on("click", function () {
      var $btn = $(this);
      request_lane_action(frm, parseInt($btn.data("lane"), 10), $btn.data("action"));
    });
    container.find(".pts3-btn-stop").on("click", function () {
      request_abort(frm, parseInt($(this).data("lane"), 10));
    });
    container.find(".pts3-btn-reset").on("click", function () {
      reset_lane(frm, parseInt($(this).data("lane"), 10));
    });
  }

  function escape_html(s) {
    if (s == null) return "";
    const div = document.createElement("div");
    div.textContent = String(s);
    return div.innerHTML;
  }

  // -----------------------
  // 5. Live table rendering (Channel as rows: Left, Right, Diff; freqs as columns)
  // -----------------------
  function render_live_table(lane) {
    const raw = lane.live_table_json || get_cached_lane_value(arguments[1], LANE_NO, "live_table_json");
    if (!raw) return '<div class="pts3-no-data">No table data</div>';

    let data;
    try {
      data = typeof raw === "string" ? JSON.parse(raw) : raw;
    } catch (e) {
      return '<div class="pts3-no-data">Invalid JSON</div>';
    }

    if (!data || typeof data !== "object") return '<div class="pts3-no-data">No table data</div>';

    const left = data.left || {};
    const right = data.right || {};
    const diff = data.diff || {};

    const keys = [];
    const seen = {};
    Object.keys(left).forEach(function (k) {
      if (!seen[k]) { seen[k] = true; keys.push(k); }
    });
    Object.keys(right).forEach(function (k) {
      if (!seen[k]) { seen[k] = true; keys.push(k); }
    });
    Object.keys(diff).forEach(function (k) {
      if (!seen[k]) { seen[k] = true; keys.push(k); }
    });

    keys.sort(function (a, b) {
      var ha = parseInt(String(a).replace(/[^0-9]/g, ""), 10);
      var hb = parseInt(String(b).replace(/[^0-9]/g, ""), 10);
      return (isNaN(ha) ? 0 : ha) - (isNaN(hb) ? 0 : hb);
    });

    const modeKeys = Object.keys(data).filter(function (k) {
      return k !== "left" && k !== "right" && k !== "diff" && k !== "metadata" && data[k] && typeof data[k] === "object";
    });

    let html = '<table class="table table-bordered table-condensed pts3-lrd-table"><thead><tr><th>Channel</th>';
    keys.forEach(function (k) { html += "<th>" + escape_html(k) + "</th>"; });
    html += "</tr></thead><tbody>";

    html += "<tr><td>Left</td>";
    keys.forEach(function (k) { html += "<td>" + format_val(left[k]) + "</td>"; });
    html += "</tr><tr><td>Right</td>";
    keys.forEach(function (k) { html += "<td>" + format_val(right[k]) + "</td>"; });
    html += "</tr><tr><td>Diff</td>";
    keys.forEach(function (k) { html += "<td>" + format_val(diff[k]) + "</td>"; });
    html += "</tr>";

    modeKeys.forEach(function (mk) {
      const m = data[mk];
      if (m && (m.p1 != null || m.p2 != null || m.diff != null)) {
        html += "<tr><td>" + escape_html(mk) + "</td><td colspan=\"" + keys.length + "\">P1=" + format_val(m.p1) + " P2=" + format_val(m.p2) + " Diff=" + format_val(m.diff) + "</td></tr>";
      }
    });

    html += "</tbody></table>";
    return html;
  }

  function format_val(v) {
    if (v == null) return "-";
    if (typeof v === "number") return v.toFixed(2);
    return escape_html(String(v));
  }

  // -----------------------
  // 6. Live graph rendering (SVG chart + row-format table)
  // -----------------------
  // ========== EDIT CHART SETTINGS HERE ==========
  var PTS3_LIMITS = {
    sweep: { yMin: 2000, yMax: 3500, xMin: 40, xMax: 80 },
    diff:  { yMin: -150, yMax: 150, xMin: 40, xMax: 80 }
  };
  // width, height: chart size (px). axisFontSize: axis labels. legendFontSize: legend above chart.
  // lineWidth, diffLineWidth: data line thickness.
  // xMajorInterval: X major tick spacing (Hz). xMinorInterval: X minor grid (Hz).
  // yMajorCount: Y major divisions. yMinorPerMajor: minor lines between majors.
  // gridMajorWidth, gridMinorWidth, gridMinorOpacity: grid. axisWidth: axis.
  var PTS3_CHART_STYLE = {
    width: 1600, height: 700,
    padding: { top: 25, right: 25, bottom: 50, left: 150 },
    axisFontSize: 35, legendFontSize: 14,
    lineWidth: 5, diffLineWidth: 5,
    xMajorInterval: 4, xMinorInterval: 2,
    yMajorCount: 5, yMinorPerMajor: 2,
    gridMajorWidth: 2, gridMinorWidth: 2, gridMinorOpacity: .8,
    axisWidth: 4
  };
  // ==============================================
  var CHART = {
    width: PTS3_CHART_STYLE.width, height: PTS3_CHART_STYLE.height,
    padding: PTS3_CHART_STYLE.padding,
    fontSize: PTS3_CHART_STYLE.axisFontSize != null ? PTS3_CHART_STYLE.axisFontSize : 14,
    fontColor: "var(--text-color, #36414c)",
    lineLeft: "#E53935", lineRight: "#2196F3", lineDiff: "#4CAF50",
    axisColor: "rgba(74,74,74,0.5)",
    gridColor: "rgba(74,74,74,0.35)"
  };

  function render_live_graph(lane, frm) {
    const raw = lane.live_graph_json || get_cached_lane_value(frm, LANE_NO, "live_graph_json");
    if (!raw) return '<div class="pts3-no-data">No graph data</div>';

    let data;
    try {
      data = typeof raw === "string" ? JSON.parse(raw) : raw;
    } catch (e) {
      return '<div class="pts3-no-data">Invalid JSON</div>';
    }

    if (!data || typeof data !== "object") return '<div class="pts3-no-data">No graph data</div>';

    const type = data.type || "sweep";
    const freqs = data.freqs || [];
    const left = data.left || [];
    const right = data.right || [];
    const diff = data.diff || [];

    if (freqs.length === 0 && type === "sweep") {
      return '<div class="pts3-no-data">No sweep points yet</div>';
    }

    var out = "";
    if (freqs.length >= 2) {
      var chartResult = render_sweep_chart_svg(freqs, left, right, diff);
      var diffChartSvg = render_diff_chart_svg(freqs, diff);
      out += '<div class="pts3-charts-row">';
      var legFs = (PTS3_CHART_STYLE.legendFontSize != null ? PTS3_CHART_STYLE.legendFontSize : 13) + "px";
      out += '<div class="pts3-chart-wrap"><p style="font-size:' + legFs + ';margin:0 0 4px 0;color:' + CHART.fontColor + ';"><span style="color:' + CHART.lineLeft + '">—</span> Left &nbsp; <span style="color:' + CHART.lineRight + '">—</span> Right &nbsp; <span style="color:' + CHART.lineDiff + '">- -</span> Diff</p>' + chartResult.svg + '</div>';
      if (diffChartSvg) {
        out += '<div class="pts3-chart-wrap pts3-diff-chart-wrap"><p style="font-size:' + legFs + ';margin:0 0 4px 0;color:' + CHART.fontColor + ';"><span style="color:' + CHART.lineDiff + '">- -</span> Diff vs Hz</p>' + diffChartSvg + '</div>';
      }
      out += '</div>';
    }

    // Mode bar chart (Mode1/2/3/0: Left(P1), Right(P2), Diff)
    var modeSvg = render_mode_bar_chart_from_table(lane);
    if (modeSvg) {
      out += '<div class="pts3-chart-wrap pts3-mode-chart-wrap" style="margin-top:0.75rem;">' +
        '<p style="font-size:' + ((PTS3_CHART_STYLE.legendFontSize != null ? PTS3_CHART_STYLE.legendFontSize : 13) + "px") +
        ';margin:0 0 4px 0;color:' + CHART.fontColor + ';">' +
        '<strong>Mode Values</strong> &nbsp; ' +
        '<span style="color:' + CHART.lineLeft + '">■</span> Left(P1) &nbsp; ' +
        '<span style="color:' + CHART.lineRight + '">■</span> Right(P2) &nbsp; ' +
        '<span style="color:' + CHART.lineDiff + '">■</span> Diff' +
        '</p>' + modeSvg + '</div>';
    }
    return out;
  }

  function get_cached_lane_value(frm, lane_no, key) {
    if (!frm || !frm[PTS3_UI_CACHE_KEY]) return "";
    const ln = parseInt(lane_no, 10);
    const c = frm[PTS3_UI_CACHE_KEY][ln] || {};
    return c[key] || "";
  }

  function render_mode_bar_chart_from_table(lane) {
    const raw = lane.live_table_json;
    if (!raw) return "";
    let t;
    try { t = typeof raw === "string" ? JSON.parse(raw) : raw; } catch (e) { return ""; }
    if (!t || typeof t !== "object") return "";

    var order = ["Mode1", "Mode2", "Mode3", "Mode0"];
    var rows = [];
    for (var i = 0; i < order.length; i++) {
      var m = t[order[i]];
      if (m && typeof m === "object" && (m.p1 != null || m.p2 != null || m.diff != null)) {
        rows.push({
          label: order[i],
          p1: m.p1 != null ? Number(m.p1) : 0,
          p2: m.p2 != null ? Number(m.p2) : 0,
          diff: m.diff != null ? Number(m.diff) : 0
        });
      }
    }
    if (!rows.length) return "";
    return render_mode_bar_chart_svg(rows);
  }

  function render_mode_bar_chart_svg(rows) {
    // Uses same CHART dimensions; bars are grouped per mode
    var pw = CHART.width, ph = Math.max(320, Math.round(CHART.height * 0.45));
    var pad = { top: 20, right: 20, bottom: 45, left: CHART.padding.left };
    var gx = pad.left, gy = pad.top, gw = pw - pad.left - pad.right, gh = ph - pad.top - pad.bottom;

    var vals = [];
    for (var i = 0; i < rows.length; i++) {
      vals.push(rows[i].p1, rows[i].p2, rows[i].diff);
    }
    var vMin = Math.min(0, Math.min.apply(null, vals));
    var vMax = Math.max.apply(null, vals);
    if (!isFinite(vMin)) vMin = 0;
    if (!isFinite(vMax) || vMax === 0) vMax = 1;
    // add a little headroom
    var head = (vMax - vMin) * 0.1;
    vMax += head;
    vMin -= head;
    var vRange = (vMax - vMin) || 1;

    function y(v) { return gy + gh - ((Number(v) - vMin) / vRange) * gh; }
    function xGroup(i) { return gx + (i / Math.max(rows.length, 1)) * gw; }

    var svg = '<svg class="pts3-chart-svg" width="' + pw + '" height="' + ph + '" viewBox="0 0 ' + pw + ' ' + ph + '" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet" style="max-width:100%;height:auto;display:block;">';
    svg += '<g>';

    // Y grid + labels
    var ySteps = 5;
    for (var yi = 0; yi <= ySteps; yi++) {
      var yy = gy + gh - (yi / ySteps) * gh;
      var v = vMin + (yi / ySteps) * vRange;
      svg += '<line x1="' + gx + '" y1="' + yy + '" x2="' + (gx + gw) + '" y2="' + yy + '" stroke="' + CHART.gridColor + '" stroke-width="' + (PTS3_CHART_STYLE.gridMajorWidth || 1) + '" opacity="0.6"/>';
      svg += '<text x="' + (gx - 6) + '" y="' + (yy + 4) + '" text-anchor="end" font-size="' + CHART.fontSize + '" fill="' + CHART.fontColor + '">' + format_val(v) + '</text>';
    }

    // Zero line emphasized
    if (vMin < 0 && vMax > 0) {
      var y0 = y(0);
      svg += '<line x1="' + gx + '" y1="' + y0 + '" x2="' + (gx + gw) + '" y2="' + y0 + '" stroke="' + CHART.axisColor + '" stroke-width="' + ((PTS3_CHART_STYLE.axisWidth || 1.5) + 1) + '" opacity="0.9"/>';
    }

    // Axes
    svg += '<line x1="' + gx + '" y1="' + (gy + gh) + '" x2="' + (gx + gw) + '" y2="' + (gy + gh) + '" stroke="' + CHART.axisColor + '" stroke-width="' + (PTS3_CHART_STYLE.axisWidth || 1.5) + '"/>';
    svg += '<line x1="' + gx + '" y1="' + gy + '" x2="' + gx + '" y2="' + (gy + gh) + '" stroke="' + CHART.axisColor + '" stroke-width="' + (PTS3_CHART_STYLE.axisWidth || 1.5) + '"/>';

    // Bars
    var groupW = gw / Math.max(rows.length, 1);
    var innerPad = Math.min(18, groupW * 0.12);
    var barW = Math.max(10, (groupW - innerPad * 2) / 3.4);
    var gap = Math.max(6, barW * 0.2);
    for (var i = 0; i < rows.length; i++) {
      var baseX = gx + i * groupW + innerPad;
      var yBase = y(0);
      var items = [
        { v: rows[i].p1, color: CHART.lineLeft },
        { v: rows[i].p2, color: CHART.lineRight },
        { v: rows[i].diff, color: CHART.lineDiff }
      ];
      for (var b = 0; b < items.length; b++) {
        var v = items[b].v;
        var yy = y(v);
        var top = Math.min(yy, yBase);
        var h = Math.abs(yBase - yy);
        svg += '<rect x="' + (baseX + b * (barW + gap)) + '" y="' + top + '" width="' + barW + '" height="' + Math.max(0.5, h) + '" fill="' + items[b].color + '" opacity="0.85"/>';
      }
      // Mode label
      svg += '<text x="' + (gx + i * groupW + groupW / 2) + '" y="' + (ph - 8) + '" text-anchor="middle" font-size="' + CHART.fontSize + '" fill="' + CHART.fontColor + '">' + rows[i].label + '</text>';
    }

    svg += '</g></svg>';
    return svg;
  }

  function render_sweep_chart_svg(freqs, left, right, diff) {
    if (!freqs || freqs.length < 2) return { svg: "" };
    var L = PTS3_LIMITS.sweep || {};
    var pw = CHART.width, ph = CHART.height, pad = CHART.padding;
    var gx = pad.left, gy = pad.top, gw = pw - pad.left - pad.right, gh = ph - pad.top - pad.bottom;
    var vMin = L.yMin != null ? Number(L.yMin) : 1500;
    var vMax = L.yMax != null ? Number(L.yMax) : 3500;
    var vRange = vMax - vMin || 1;
    var freqMin = L.xMin != null ? Number(L.xMin) : 40;
    var freqMax = L.xMax != null ? Number(L.xMax) : 80;
    var freqRange = freqMax - freqMin || 1;
    function x(i) { return gx + ((Number(freqs[i]) - freqMin) / freqRange) * gw; }
    function y(v) { return gy + gh - ((Number(v) - vMin) / vRange) * gh; }
    function path(arr) {
      var pts = [];
      for (var i = 0; i < arr.length; i++) {
        if (arr[i] != null && !isNaN(Number(arr[i]))) pts.push(x(i) + "," + y(arr[i]));
      }
      return pts.length ? "M" + pts.join(" L") : "";
    }
    var pLeft = path(left), pRight = path(right), pDiff = path(diff);
    var S = PTS3_CHART_STYLE;
    var xMajor = S.xMajorInterval > 0 ? S.xMajorInterval : 6;
    var xMinor = S.xMinorInterval > 0 ? S.xMinorInterval : 2;
    var yMaj = S.yMajorCount > 0 ? S.yMajorCount : 5;
    var yMinPer = S.yMinorPerMajor > 0 ? S.yMinorPerMajor : 4;
    var gMajW = S.gridMajorWidth != null ? S.gridMajorWidth : 1;
    var gMinW = S.gridMinorWidth != null ? S.gridMinorWidth : 0.5;
    var gMinOp = S.gridMinorOpacity != null ? S.gridMinorOpacity : 0.8;
    var axW = S.axisWidth != null ? S.axisWidth : 6;
    var lw = S.lineWidth != null ? S.lineWidth : 4;
    var dlw = S.diffLineWidth != null ? S.diffLineWidth : lw;
    var svg = '<svg class="pts3-chart-svg" width="' + pw + '" height="' + ph + '" viewBox="0 0 ' + pw + ' ' + ph + '" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet" style="max-width:100%;height:auto;display:block;">';
    svg += '<g>';
    for (var tickFreq = freqMin; tickFreq <= freqMax; tickFreq += xMinor) {
      var xx = gx + ((Number(tickFreq) - freqMin) / freqRange) * gw;
      if (xx >= gx - 1 && xx <= gx + gw + 1) {
        var isMajor = (tickFreq - freqMin) % xMajor === 0;
        svg += '<line x1="' + xx + '" y1="' + (gy + gh) + '" x2="' + xx + '" y2="' + gy + '" stroke="' + CHART.gridColor + '" stroke-width="' + (isMajor ? gMajW : gMinW) + '" opacity="' + (isMajor ? 0.5 : gMinOp) + '"/>';
        if (isMajor) svg += '<text x="' + xx + '" y="' + (ph - 2) + '" text-anchor="middle" font-size="' + CHART.fontSize + '" fill="' + CHART.fontColor + '">' + tickFreq + '</text>';
      }
    }
var stepY = 250;
    var startY = Math.ceil(vMin / stepY) * stepY;
    var endY = Math.floor(vMax / stepY) * stepY;
    for (var v = startY; v <= endY; v += stepY) {
      var yy = y(v);
      var isZero = Number(v) === 0;
      svg += '<line x1="' + gx + '" y1="' + yy + '" x2="' + (gx + gw) + '" y2="' + yy + '" stroke="' + (isZero ? CHART.axisColor : CHART.gridColor) + '" stroke-width="' + (isZero ? (axW + 1) : gMajW) + '" opacity="' + (isZero ? 0.95 : 0.8) + '"/>';
      svg += '<text x="' + (gx - 6) + '" y="' + (yy + 3) + '" text-anchor="end" font-size="' + CHART.fontSize + '" fill="' + CHART.fontColor + '">' + format_val(v) + '</text>';
    }
    svg += '<line x1="' + gx + '" y1="' + (gy + gh) + '" x2="' + (gx + gw) + '" y2="' + (gy + gh) + '" stroke="' + CHART.axisColor + '" stroke-width="' + axW + '"/>';
    svg += '<line x1="' + gx + '" y1="' + gy + '" x2="' + gx + '" y2="' + (gy + gh) + '" stroke="' + CHART.axisColor + '" stroke-width="' + axW + '"/>';
    if (pLeft) svg += '<path d="' + pLeft + '" fill="none" stroke="' + CHART.lineLeft + '" stroke-width="' + lw + '"/>';
    if (pRight) svg += '<path d="' + pRight + '" fill="none" stroke="' + CHART.lineRight + '" stroke-width="' + lw + '"/>';
    if (pDiff) svg += '<path d="' + pDiff + '" fill="none" stroke="' + CHART.lineDiff + '" stroke-width="' + dlw + '" stroke-dasharray="4,2"/>';
    svg += '</g></svg>';
    return { svg: svg };
  }

  function render_diff_chart_svg(freqs, diff) {
    if (!freqs || freqs.length < 2 || !diff || diff.length < 2) return "";
    var L = PTS3_LIMITS.diff || {};
    var pw = CHART.width, ph = CHART.height, pad = CHART.padding;
    var gx = pad.left, gy = pad.top, gw = pw - pad.left - pad.right, gh = ph - pad.top - pad.bottom;
    var vMin = L.yMin != null ? Number(L.yMin) : -160;
    var vMax = L.yMax != null ? Number(L.yMax) : 160;
    var vRange = vMax - vMin || 1;
    var freqMin = L.xMin != null ? Number(L.xMin) : 40;
    var freqMax = L.xMax != null ? Number(L.xMax) : 80;
    var freqRange = freqMax - freqMin || 1;
    function x(i) { var f = Number(freqs[i]) || freqMin; return gx + ((f - freqMin) / freqRange) * gw; }
    function y(v) { return gy + gh - ((Number(v) - vMin) / vRange) * gh; }
    function path(arr) {
      var pts = [];
      for (var i = 0; i < arr.length; i++) {
        if (arr[i] != null && !isNaN(Number(arr[i]))) pts.push(x(i) + "," + y(arr[i]));
      }
      return pts.length ? "M" + pts.join(" L") : "";
    }
    var pDiff = path(diff);
    if (!pDiff) return "";
    var S = PTS3_CHART_STYLE;
    var xMajor = S.xMajorInterval > 0 ? S.xMajorInterval : 4;
    var xMinor = S.xMinorInterval > 0 ? S.xMinorInterval : 2;
    var yMaj = S.yMajorCount > 0 ? S.yMajorCount : 5;
    var yMinPer = S.yMinorPerMajor > 0 ? S.yMinorPerMajor : 2;
    var gMajW = S.gridMajorWidth != null ? S.gridMajorWidth : 1;
    var gMinW = S.gridMinorWidth != null ? S.gridMinorWidth : 0.5;
    var gMinOp = S.gridMinorOpacity != null ? S.gridMinorOpacity : 0.3;
    var axW = S.axisWidth != null ? S.axisWidth : 1.5;
    var dlw = S.diffLineWidth != null ? S.diffLineWidth : (S.lineWidth != null ? S.lineWidth : 2);
    var svg = '<svg class="pts3-chart-svg" width="' + pw + '" height="' + ph + '" viewBox="0 0 ' + pw + ' ' + ph + '" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet" style="max-width:100%;height:auto;display:block;">';
    svg += '<g>';
    for (var tickFreq = freqMin; tickFreq <= freqMax; tickFreq += xMinor) {
      var xx = gx + ((Number(tickFreq) - freqMin) / freqRange) * gw;
      if (xx >= gx - 1 && xx <= gx + gw + 1) {
        var isMajor = (tickFreq - freqMin) % xMajor === 0;
        svg += '<line x1="' + xx + '" y1="' + (gy + gh) + '" x2="' + xx + '" y2="' + gy + '" stroke="' + CHART.gridColor + '" stroke-width="' + (isMajor ? gMajW : gMinW) + '" opacity="' + (isMajor ? 0.5 : gMinOp) + '"/>';
        if (isMajor) svg += '<text x="' + xx + '" y="' + (ph - 2) + '" text-anchor="middle" font-size="' + CHART.fontSize + '" fill="' + CHART.fontColor + '">' + tickFreq + '</text>';
      }
    }
    var stepY = 40;
    var startY = Math.ceil(vMin / stepY) * stepY;
    var endY = Math.floor(vMax / stepY) * stepY;
    for (var v = startY; v <= endY; v += stepY) {
      var yy = y(v);
      var isZero = Number(v) === 0;
      svg += '<line x1="' + gx + '" y1="' + yy + '" x2="' + (gx + gw) + '" y2="' + yy + '" stroke="' + (isZero ? CHART.axisColor : CHART.gridColor) + '" stroke-width="' + (isZero ? (axW + 1) : gMajW) + '" opacity="' + (isZero ? 0.95 : 0.8) + '"/>';
      svg += '<text x="' + (gx - 6) + '" y="' + (yy + 3) + '" text-anchor="end" font-size="' + CHART.fontSize + '" fill="' + CHART.fontColor + '">' + format_val(v) + '</text>';
    }
    svg += '<line x1="' + gx + '" y1="' + (gy + gh) + '" x2="' + (gx + gw) + '" y2="' + (gy + gh) + '" stroke="' + CHART.axisColor + '" stroke-width="' + axW + '"/>';
    svg += '<line x1="' + gx + '" y1="' + gy + '" x2="' + gx + '" y2="' + (gy + gh) + '" stroke="' + CHART.axisColor + '" stroke-width="' + axW + '"/>';
    svg += '<path d="' + pDiff + '" fill="none" stroke="' + CHART.lineDiff + '" stroke-width="' + dlw + '" stroke-dasharray="4,2"/>';
    svg += '</g></svg>';
    return svg;
  }

})();

You *can* do scope header + VISA initialization at connector start — that’s exactly what we added (connector sends `cmd:"init"` to `pts3_runner_daemon` on startup).  

If you still see logs like **`START AUTO_PTS3v17.py`** when you press **Step Sweep / Mode**, it means **the connector is not using the daemon** and is **falling back to subprocess** (cold start), so it re-initializes every job.

### Why it’s still initializing on button press
- **Connector can’t reach the daemon** at `127.0.0.1:8765` (wrong port, daemon not running, blocked, different host).
- Or **you didn’t restart the connector after updating it**, so it’s still the old version (no warmup / no runner usage).
- Or the daemon is running but **not from the same environment / path**, so it can’t load `Scope_header_v2.py` (then init fails and connector falls back).

### What to verify on the test PC (fast checklist)
1. **Start daemon manually once** (from the same folder as `Scope_header_v2.py`):
   - `python pts3_runner_daemon.py`
   - It should print: `"[RUNNER] Started on 127.0.0.1:8765"`

2. **Restart the connector** and look at the *first* console lines:
   - You must see something like:  
     - `Preparing oscilloscope (runner init on 127.0.0.1:8765)…`  
     - `Oscilloscope pre-initialized (runner): USB...`

3. When you press **Step Sweep / Mode**, you must see in connector logs:
   - `Using runner 127.0.0.1:8765 (scope session kept hot)`
   - And you should **NOT** see `START AUTO_PTS3v17.py` (that only appears in subprocess fallback).

### If you want “never re-init per job”
Tell me and I’ll change the connector behavior to **hard-require the daemon**:
- If runner is not reachable → mark lane **Failed** with clear error (instead of spawning `AUTO_PTS3v17.py`).

### One more common gotcha (Scope header path)
`pts3_runner_daemon.py` loads `Scope_header_v2.py` from its own folder by default. If your `Scope_header_v2.py` is elsewhere, set:
- `PTS3_SCOPE_HEADER_PATH=C:\path\to\Scope_header_v2.py`

If you paste the **first ~30 lines of the connector startup log** (right after you start it) and the **daemon startup log**, I can tell you immediately which of the above is failing.

## Changes made

1. **Default script** – Connector now uses `AUTO_PTS3v17.py` instead of v16.

## Why you might see no data

### 1. Station name mismatch

**Station** in PTS3 Test must match the connector’s PC name exactly.

On connector startup you’ll see something like:
```
[PTS3] Station field in PTS3 Test must exactly match: DESKTOP-AKC688N
```

Use that exact value in the Station field (e.g. `DESKTOP-AKC688N` or `PC-DESKTOP-AKC688N`).

### 2. Connector not finding the job

If you never see `Found 1 requested job(s)` or `Claimed...`:

- Station does not match the connector PC name.
- API key lacks read permission on PTS3 Test.

### 3. AUTO_PTS3 needs hardware

Step sweep uses:

- A `Step_sweep` folder with WAV files (40, 42, …, 80 Hz).
- VISA/Oscilloscope hardware.

Without these, the script may fail or emit no sweep data.

---

2. In PTS3 Test, set Station to that exact value.

4. If those appear but no sweep data, check that `Step_sweep` exists and VISA/scope are configured.

A troubleshooting guide is in `41_PTS3_CONNECTOR_NO_DATA_TROUBLESHOOTING.md`.

### AI  ``

That log is **normal** for the current defaults.

**What’s going on**

- **`mode0`** is treated as a **mode** job (`mode1`…`mode0`).
- By design, **`should_use_runner()` is false** for those unless you opt in, so the connector runs **`AUTO_PTS3v17.py --cli` in a subprocess** (so 80 Hz audio usually works from the user session).
- So **“Runner skipped for this job”** is expected for a lone **Mode 0** request.

**If you want this job to use `pts3_runner_daemon` instead**

In PowerShell **before** starting the connector:

```powershell
$env:PTS3_USE_RUNNER_FOR_MODES = "1"
& "C:/Users/H P/AppData/Local/Programs/Python/Python313/python.exe" "d:/PTS3_Modified/PTS3_Modified/pts3_connector.py"
```

**If you want “Submit (runner) → then Mode 1–0 on the runner” (continuous 80 Hz in the daemon)**

1. Run **Submit** so it uses the runner (default for `submit`).
2. Set:

```powershell
$env:PTS3_COHERENT_RUNNER_MODES = "1"
```

3. Then run **Mode** jobs for the **same** PCB serial (connector remembers after a successful runner Submit).

**Note:** The daemon often has **no audible** 80 Hz to Bluetooth/speakers; subprocess is usually chosen so tone is heard. Use the runner for modes only if you’re OK with that tradeoff or you’ve fixed audio routing for the daemon.

No bug in the log—it’s the connector telling you which path it chose and how to switch it.

### AI  ``

Fixed the real root cause and redeployed.

### Why it was happening
Your `PTS3 Test` page shows data because it reads **lane live fields** (`live_graph_json` / `live_table_json`) while the run is happening.

But the `PTS3 Result` doc was being saved from `save_final_result(result=...)`, and in some cases Frappe was turning nested dicts inside `result` into **stringified Python dicts** (single quotes). That makes the saved `final_graph_json` / `left_right_diff_summary_json` **not valid JSON**, so the Result page renders **“No sweep data”**.

### What I changed (server-side)
In `pts3_api_server_script.py` → `save_final_result`:

- If `result_json` is provided (connector sends it), we now **prefer it as the source of truth** and only fill missing keys from `result`.
- This guarantees we save **real JSON** (not Python dict strings).

### Deployed
I redeployed the updated `pts3_api` Server Script to ERPNext (`frontend`).

### What to do now (fast verification)
1. Run **one new Step Sweep** (new Run ID).
2. Open the new **PTS3 Result**.
3. You should see:
   - Step Sweep charts populated
   - Left/Right/Diff summary table populated
   - Artifacts should no longer show a Python-dict “Legacy path …” style string.

Old result rows won’t auto-fix; they were saved already. If you want, I can add a one-time backfill to repair old rows using lane live JSON or Excel.

Tuple assignment like `graph, table = fill_lrd_from_sweep_graph(...)` is compiled in a way that needs **`_unpack_sequence_`**, which is **not** provided in that environment → **`NameError: name '_unpack_sequence_' is not defined`**.

**Change:** Drop tuple unpacking and use a single return value + indexing:

```python
lrd_out = fill_lrd_from_sweep_graph(r, graph, table)
graph = lrd_out[0]
table = lrd_out[1]
```

(and the same pattern for the second call with `lrd_out2`).

**In the repo:** `pts3_api_server_script.py` is updated and a short comment was added at the top: **no** `a, b = func()` in Server Scripts.

**What you should do:** Paste the updated `pts3_api_server_script.py` into the Server Script **pts3_api** in Frappe and save, then run again.

If anything else blows up, the next place to check is other unpacks (e.g. `for k, v in ...`); we can rewrite those if needed.

Here’s what was implemented and how it maps to your desired pattern.

### Format

**`{pcb_serial_slug}_{short_action}_{series}`**

- **Serial**: taken from lane 1 `pcb_serial_no`, slugified (letters/digits, other chars → `_`, max 60 chars). Empty → `UNKNOWN`.
- **Sweep vs mode**: `step_sweep` → `sweep`, `full_test` → `full`, `mode1` / `mode2` / … stay as-is.
- **Series**: Frappe’s `{#####}` counter (same idea as the old numeric tail).

Example names: `acvc_sweep_00001`, `SN12345_mode1_00002`.

Slashes are **not** used in the **name** (they’re awkward in URLs and links). You still get a clear **sweep vs mode** segment.

### Repo changes

1. **`create_pts3_doctypes_v1.py`**  
   - New **PTS3 Test** installs use  
     `autoname = "format:{name_serial_slug}_{name_op_short}_{#####}"`  
     and **`naming_rule = "Expression"`**, with hidden fields **`name_serial_slug`** and **`name_op_short`.**  
   - **`naming_series`** is no longer used for new installs from this script.  
   - **`ensure_pts3_test_naming_format()`** adds the two fields, switches the autoname format, and clears **`reqd`** on legacy **`naming_series`** if it still exists.

2. **`PTS3_Test_Client_Script.js`**  
   - **`before_save`** fills **`name_serial_slug`** / **`name_op_short`** from lane 1 (same lane as the rest of the UI).  
   - Those fields are **hidden** in the form.

### What you do on the server

1. Run the bench script (or paste your `exec(open(...))` path) so **`ensure_pts3_test_naming_format()`** runs.  
2. **Clear cache** (`bench --site … clear-cache` or from Desk).  
3. **Update** the PTS3 Test **Client Script** in Frappe from the repo file.

**Manual DocType check** (if you prefer not to run the script):

- **Naming** → **Auto Name**:  
  `format:{name_serial_slug}_{name_op_short}_{#####}`  
- **Naming Rule**: **Expression**  
- Add **Data** fields **`name_serial_slug`** and **`name_op_short`** (can be hidden).

### AI  ``

Identifying the issue: the connector warms the runner (scope stays open), then mode jobs run `AUTO_PTS3v17.py --cli` in a subprocess that calls `list_resources()` and `open_resource()` — a second open of the same USB device while the runner holds it, causing NI-VISA access violations on Python 3.13.

Implementing: (1) make runner warmup opt-in so we don't hold the scope by default when modes use subprocess; (2) inject `PTS3_VISA_RESOURCE` into the connector process after successful warmup so CLI skips `list_resources`; (3) warn when `list_resources` is about to run without `PTS3_VISA_RESOURCE`.

### Name pattern

New **PTS3 Result** rows get names like:

- `pts3_<serial_slug>_sweep_<n>` — for **`step_sweep`** and **`submit`**
- `pts3_<serial_slug>_mode_<n>` — for **`mode1`**, **`mode2`**, **`mode3`**, **`mode0`**, **`full_test`**

`<serial_slug>` comes from PCB serial (letters, digits, `_`, `-` only; other characters become `_`; max 80 chars; empty → `UNKNOWN`).

`<n>` is a **per-(serial, sweep|mode)** counter: it looks at existing `tabPTS3 Result` names with the same prefix and uses **max + 1** (with a small retry loop if there’s a clash).

2. **`EXAMPLES/CHARGPT  TRIAL/PTS3 test/PTS3 test/pts3_api_server_script.py`**

Summary of what was implemented:

## Connector Implementation Summary

### Created Files

1. **`pts3_connector.py`** – Connector script that:
   - Polls ERP for Requested lanes using Frappe resource API + `get_status_snapshot`
   - Claims lanes via `claim_lane` (status → Queued)
   - Launches `AUTO_PTS3v16.py --cli` with mode, serial, lane_no, run_id
   - Sets status to Running via `update_lane_fields` after subprocess start
   - Parses stdout line-by-line, ignores non-JSON lines
   - Handles events: status, sweep_point, mode_progress, mode_point, mode_complete, completed, failed, log
   - Accumulates live_graph_json and live_table_json for sweep and modes
   - Sends heartbeat updates during run
   - Calls `mark_lane_failed` if subprocess launch fails after claim
   - Calls `save_final_result` on success (with operation, datetime, left_right_diff_summary)
   - Calls `mark_lane_failed` on failure
   - Terminates subprocess and calls `abort_lane` when `abort_requested` is set

2. **`23_CONNECTOR_DEPLOYMENT_AND_TESTS.md`** – Deployment and test guide with:
   - Config (env vars)
   - Local test procedure
   - Assumptions
   - Remaining ERP dependency gaps

### Polling Method (No New Endpoint)

- Uses Frappe resource API: `GET /api/resource/PTS3 Test?filters=[["target_pc","=",TARGET_PC]]` to list PTS3 Test docs
- For each doc, calls `get_status_snapshot(docname)` to get lane details
- Extracts lanes with `lane_action_status == "Requested"`
- Processes one job per poll cycle to avoid overlap

### Other Change

- **`11_CONNECTOR_ENDPOINTS.md`** – `request_lane_action` response updated to remove `run_id` (only `claim_lane` returns it)

### Config Required

| Variable | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `PTS3_ERP_URL` | ERP base URL |
| `PTS3_API_KEY` / `PTS3_API_SECRET` | Token auth |
| `PTS3_TARGET_PC` | Must match PTS3 Test.target_pc (default: hostname) |
| `PTS3_SCRIPT_PATH` | Path to AUTO_PTS3v16.py |
| `PTS3_PYTHON_PATH` | Python interpreter |

### Assumptions

- Frappe resource list API is enabled
- `AUTO_PTS3v16.py --cli` runs standalone
- Working directory is the script directory (for Step_sweep/, PCB_READINGS/)
- `lane_action` uses internal codes (step_sweep, mode1, etc.)

### Known Limitation

- Abort is checked only when stdout lines arrive; during long captures (e.g. 5s mode) abort may be delayed until the next event.

### What was going wrong

That message is from **`AUTO_PTS3v17.py`**, not from `pts3_connector.py`. On **Python 3.13**, the first time the app needs the scope it calls **`ensure_visa()`**. If **`PTS3_VISA_RESOURCE`** is not set and there is no usable **`PTS3_VISA_RESOURCE.txt`**, it prints that **`[ERROR]`** line.

Your copy under **`D:\PTS3_Modified\PTS3_Modified\`** did not have **`_load_pts3_visa_resource_file()`**, so the script never read a txt file before failing.

### What we changed in the repo

In  
`PCB_IQC_ERPNext_Project\EXAMPLES\CHARGPT  TRIAL\PTS3 test\AUTO_PTS3v17.py` we restored:

- **`_visa_txt_search_dirs()`** / **`_load_pts3_visa_resource_file()`** — loads **`PTS3_VISA_RESOURCE.txt`** from:
  - folder of **`AUTO_PTS3v17.py`**
  - current working directory (if different)
  - **`%LOCALAPPDATA%\PTS3\`**
  - **`%USERPROFILE%\.pts3\`**
- **`ensure_visa()`** — calls **`_load_pts3_visa_resource_file()`** first, then applies the Python **3.13** rules and optional **`PTS3_VISA_ALLOW_ENUM=1`**.

There is also **`PTS3_VISA_RESOURCE.txt.example`** in the same **`PTS3 test`** folder as a template.

**Copy the updated `AUTO_PTS3v17.py` to `D:\PTS3_Modified\PTS3_Modified\`** (replace the file there).

### What you must do on the bench PC

1. In **`D:\PTS3_Modified\PTS3_Modified\`**, create **`PTS3_VISA_RESOURCE.txt`** (not only `.example`).

2. Put **exactly one** non-comment line (from **NI MAX** for your scope), for example:

   `USB0::0x0699::0x03C4::C012223::INSTR`

3. Run **`AUTO_PTS3v17.py`** again. You should see:

   `[PTS3] Loaded PTS3_VISA_RESOURCE from D:\PTS3_Modified\PTS3_Modified\PTS3_VISA_RESOURCE.txt`

**Or** set a persistent user variable and open a **new** terminal:

`setx PTS3_VISA_RESOURCE "USB0::....::INSTR"`

**Temporary unsafe option** (can crash):  
`set PTS3_VISA_ALLOW_ENUM=1` before running, then try enumeration on 3.13.

---

**Note:** First run showed only **mainloop closing** with no VISA error; the second run hit the error when something triggered **`ensure_visa()`** (e.g. **Save / Step Sweep / Mode** or shutdown path). After the txt file or env is set, that path should succeed.

- Uses Frappe resource API: `GET /api/resource/PTS3 Test?filters=[["target_pc","=",TARGET_PC]]` to list PTS3 Test docs
- For each doc, calls `get_status_snapshot(docname)` to get lane details
- Extracts lanes with `lane_action_status == "Requested"`
- Processes one job per poll cycle to avoid overlap

### Other Change

- **`11_CONNECTOR_ENDPOINTS.md`** – `request_lane_action` response updated to remove `run_id` (only `claim_lane` returns it)

### Config Required

| Variable | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `PTS3_ERP_URL` | ERP base URL |
| `PTS3_API_KEY` / `PTS3_API_SECRET` | Token auth |
| `PTS3_TARGET_PC` | Must match PTS3 Test.target_pc (default: hostname) |
| `PTS3_SCRIPT_PATH` | Path to AUTO_PTS3v16.py |
| `PTS3_PYTHON_PATH` | Python interpreter |

### Assumptions

- Frappe resource list API is enabled
- `AUTO_PTS3v16.py --cli` runs standalone
- Working directory is the script directory (for Step_sweep/, PCB_READINGS/)
- `lane_action` uses internal codes (step_sweep, mode1, etc.)

### Known Limitation

- Abort is checked only when stdout lines arrive; during long captures (e.g. 5s mode) abort may be delayed until the next event.

## Part 2 - Exact Final Doctype Specification

### Naming Strategy

- **fieldname**: snake_case, no spaces
- **label**: Human-readable, may have spaces
- **DocType names**: PTS3 Test, PTS3 Lane, PTS3 Result, PTS3 Frequency Row
- **Module**: PCB IQC or custom app module

### Field Categories

- **Live runtime only**: Updated during run, cleared or overwritten on reset
- **Final saved result**: Snapshot after completion, persists
- **Operator UI support**: Used for Left/Right/Diff display, graph render
- **Connector control**: Written by connector or server script for connector flow

## What’s wrong

- `opv` is only set **inside** `if existing:` (when you’re **updating** an existing **PTS3 Result**).
- After that, the script always runs the block that starts with **“Do NOT overwrite sweep JSON…”** and uses **`if opv == "step_sweep"`**.
- When there is **no** existing result yet (`else:` → **new** PTS3 Result), the script **never** sets `opv`, so Python raises **`NameError: name 'opv' is not defined`**.

So the bug is: **`opv` must exist for both “update existing” and “create new”.**

---

## What to do (one fix)

**1. Add this *before* `if existing:`** (right after the `ap_str` block, same indent as `if existing:`):

```python
                        opv = (operation or "").strip()
```

**2. Delete the old line inside `if existing:`** that only says:

```python
                            opv = (operation or "").strip()
```

(so you don’t set `opv` twice).

After the change it should look like:

```text
                        ... ap_str handling ends ...

                        opv = (operation or "").strip()
                        if existing:
                            d = frappe.get_doc("PTS3 Result", existing)
                            if opv == "step_sweep" or opv == "submit":
                                ...
```

**3.** Save the Server Script, then run **`bench clear-cache`** (or your site’s equivalent).

**4. (Optional)** Change `PTS3_API_VERSION` (e.g. to `v3`) so you can see in API responses that the new script is live.

### Part 1 – Backend API (`pts3_book_api`)

#### 1.1. Whitelisted API method

Create a small Python module in your PTS3 app, e.g.  
`pts3/pts3/doctype/pts3_result/pts3_book_api.py`:

```python
import frappe

@frappe.whitelist()
def get_pts3_book(pcb_serial_no: str, limit: int = 20, offset: int = 0):
    """Return grouped history for one PCB serial.

    Input:
      pcb_serial_no (str)
      limit (int)
      offset (int)

    Output:
      {
        "pcb_serial_no": "...",
        "run_count": int,
        "latest_run": {...} or None,
        "runs": [ {...}, ... ]
      }
    """
    pcb_serial_no = (pcb_serial_no or "").strip()
    if not pcb_serial_no:
        return {
            "pcb_serial_no": "",
            "run_count": 0,
            "latest_run": None,
            "runs": []
        }

    # Count
    run_count = frappe.db.count(
        "PTS3 Result",
        filters={"pcb_serial_no": pcb_serial_no}
    )

    if not run_count:
        return {
            "pcb_serial_no": pcb_serial_no,
            "run_count": 0,
            "latest_run": None,
            "runs": []
        }

    # Newest first
    fields = [
        "name",
        "datetime",
        "operation",
        "pass_fail",
        "dominant_channel",
        "max_value",
        "run_id",
    ]

    runs = frappe.get_all(
        "PTS3 Result",
        filters={"pcb_serial_no": pcb_serial_no},
        fields=fields,
        order_by="datetime desc, creation desc",
        limit_start=int(offset or 0),
        limit_page_length=int(limit or 20),
    )

    # Latest run = first row from same ordering, independent of pagination
    latest = frappe.get_all(
        "PTS3 Result",
        filters={"pcb_serial_no": pcb_serial_no},
        fields=fields,
        order_by="datetime desc, creation desc",
        limit_start=0,
        limit_page_length=1,
    )
    latest_run = latest[0] if latest else None

    return {
        "pcb_serial_no": pcb_serial_no,
        "run_count": run_count,
        "latest_run": latest_run,
        "runs": runs,
    }
```

Here’s what was going wrong and what we changed.

## 1. **Scope readings were 0 in software (ERP log)**

The Tek driver was sending **`*CLS`** on **every** `configure_for_frequency()` (once per sweep step). On many TBS scopes that **clears measurement state**, so **`MEASUrement:IMMed:VALue?`** often stays **0.0** until things settle—while the **screen** can still look fine.

**Updates in `Scope_header_v2.py` (both copies):**

- **`*CLS`** only if you set **`PTS3_SCOPE_CLS=1`** (off by default).
- **Default coupling** is **`DC`** (override with **`PTS3_SCOPE_COUPLING=AC`** if you need AC).
- After scale/trigger setup, **`*OPC?`** so the instrument finishes before measuring.
- **`_measure`**: short delay after setting type, then **a second read** if the first value is 0.

Together, that should align **SCPI numbers** with what you see on the scope.

---

## 2. **ERP looked “empty” / no Excel / sweep from connector**

For **`step_sweep`**, the connector **used the runner daemon** by default. The daemon:

- Does **not** write the **`PCB_READINGS\…xlsx`** file the CLI writes.
- Sends **`artifact_paths`** as empty → **PTS3 Result** shows **no Excel / artifacts**.
- Still had the same **`read_all`** path (zeros made tables all **0.00**).

**Update in `pts3_connector.py` (both copies):**

- **`step_sweep`** now uses **`AUTO_PTS3v17.py --cli` in a subprocess** by default (same as your standalone test): **Excel + `artifact_paths`** go to ERP like the GUI/CLI.
- To use the **daemon** for sweep again (hot scope, no Excel from worker):  
  **`PTS3_USE_RUNNER_FOR_SWEEP=1`**

| `PTS3 test\PTS3 test\pts3_connector.py` | `step_sweep` → subprocess unless `PTS3_USE_RUNNER_FOR_SWEEP=1` |

### AI  ``

Here’s what was going wrong and what we changed.

### What was happening
Pressing **Step sweep** / **Mode** in ERP starts a **new** `AUTO_PTS3v17.py` process when **`pts3_runner_daemon` isn’t used**. Every run then pays the full cost: Python start, imports (Sheets, Tk, etc.), PyVISA discovery, and opening the scope — then it can play tones and read the scope. That matches your log.

### What we want
Keep **one long-lived process** that holds the **VISA session**, and have the **connector** open the scope **before** operators rely on it:

1. **`pts3_runner_daemon.py`**  
   - New commands: `init`, `scope_init`, `warm`, `warmup`  
   - They only call `ScopeSession.ensure_connected(...)` and emit  
     `{"type":"init_complete","ok":true,"resource":"..."}`  
   - The scope stays open in that process for later `step_sweep` / `mode*`.

2. **`pts3_connector.py`**  
   - On startup (before the poll loop): **`prepare_scope_for_station()`**  
     - Optionally **`PTS3_AUTO_START_RUNNER=1`**: starts `pts3_runner_daemon.py` if nothing is listening on the port.  
     - Sends **`{"cmd":"init"}`** to the runner (with retries so auto-start can finish).  
   - When a job runs, it still **prefers the runner** so you don’t spawn a cold `AUTO_PTS3v17` each time.

### What you should do on the test PC
1. **Recommended:** Run the daemon when the PC logs in (Task Scheduler shortcut or batch), **or** set:
   - `PTS3_AUTO_START_RUNNER=1`  
   so the connector starts the daemon for you.
2. Restart the **connector** and confirm logs like:
   - `[PTS3] Oscilloscope pre-initialized (runner): USB0::...`
   - On a job: `[PTS3] Using runner 127.0.0.1:8765 (scope session kept hot)`
3. If you still see **`START AUTO_PTS3v17.py`** and **Google Sheets** on each job, the runner isn’t reachable — fix port/firewall or path to `pts3_runner_daemon.py`.

**Note:** `AUTO_PTS3v17.py` is only “instant” for music + reads when jobs go through the **runner**. A subprocess run will always re-initialize VISA for that process; the runner is what makes the scope **ready before** and **between** button presses.

## Why this happens every time

Frappe **14** loads Desk Pages in two steps:

1. It loads the **Page** record from the database (`pts3-book`).
2. It calls **`load_assets()`**, which does **`os.listdir(...)`** on the **on-disk** folder for that page.

For a Core page named `pts3-book`, that path is:

`apps/frappe/frappe/core/page/pts3_book/`

(`pts3-book` → folder name **`pts3_book`** via `scrub()`.)

Your **database** already has the Page (menu / route works until load), but **that folder (or `pts3_book.js`) is missing on the server**, so **`listdir` raises `FileNotFoundError`** — every time you open `#pts3-book`.

Common causes:

- Page was created **only in Desk** (Customize → Page) **without** copying JS under `frappe/core/page/pts3_book/`.
- You ran an installer that **updated the Page doc** but **never ran** the step that **writes the file on disk** (or it ran on another machine / container).
- **Bench update / new container** wiped `sites` assets but the Page row remained, or the opposite: DB migrated without the repo files.

---

## Fix (on the **bench host**, where `apps/frappe` lives)

**Option A — use your existing installer (recommended)**  

Copy `pts3_book.js` (and the folder) to the server, then in **`bench --site <yoursite> console`**:

```python
ASSET_DIR = "/path/on/server/to/folder/containing/pts3_book.js"
exec(open(ASSET_DIR + "/pts3_bench_install.py").read())
install_pts3_book_page(ASSET_DIR)
```

That script **`makedirs`** `.../core/page/pts3_book/` and writes **`pts3_book.js`** there (see `pts3_bench_install.py` lines 55–65).

**Option B — manual**

```bash
mkdir -p apps/frappe/frappe/core/page/pts3_book
# copy your pts3_book.js to:
# apps/frappe/frappe/core/page/pts3_book/pts3_book.js
```

Then:

```bash
bench --site <yoursite> clear-cache
```

**Option C — from your PC project**  

If you use `PATCH_PTS3_BOOK_F14_DISK.py` / `INSTALL_PTS3_BOOK_AND_API_VIA_AUTO_EXECUTOR.py` against the right site, they exist **for the same reason**: create that directory + file on the server.

---

## After it works

- Opening **`#pts3-book`** should stop throwing **`FileNotFoundError`** as long as that path stays on disk across deploys (bake it into your **Docker image** or **ansible** if you use containers).

**Summary:** The error is not random — the **Page row exists, the Core page directory on disk does not.** Creating `apps/frappe/frappe/core/page/pts3_book/` and placing **`pts3_book.js`** there fixes it permanently until something removes that tree again.

## `PTS3_CHART_STYLE` – editable settings

```javascript
var PTS3_CHART_STYLE = {
  width: 1100, height: 480,
  padding: { top: 25, right: 25, bottom: 50, left: 65 },
  fontSize: 14,
  lineWidth: 2.5, diffLineWidth: 2.5,
  xMajorInterval: 4, xMinorInterval: 2,
```

| Setting | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| **width, height** | Chart size in pixels |
| **lineWidth** | Left/Right line thickness |
| **diffLineWidth** | Diff line thickness |
| **xMajorInterval** | X-axis major tick spacing (Hz), e.g. 4 → 40, 44, 48… |
| **xMinorInterval** | X-axis minor grid spacing (Hz), e.g. 2 → grid every 2 Hz |
| **yMajorCount** | Number of Y-axis major divisions |
| **yMinorPerMajor** | Minor grid lines between each major |
| **gridMajorWidth** | Major grid line thickness |
| **gridMinorWidth** | Minor grid line thickness |
| **gridMinorOpacity** | Minor grid opacity (0–1) |
| **axisWidth** | Axis line thickness |

Adjust these values in `PTS3_CHART_STYLE` to change chart size, grid, and line thickness.

### AI  ``

Here is what those console lines mean and what to do.

### What the statuses mean

1. **`Running` → `Failed`**  
   The bench run ended in failure (e.g. VISA / `ensure_visa`). ERP sets the lane to **Failed**.

2. **`auto-refresh stopped (lane no longer active)`**  
   The client only polls while status is **Requested**, **Queued**, or **Running**. After **Failed** (or **Done** / **Idle**), it stops the timer so you are not polling forever.

3. **`status=Requested` with `live_graph_len=0`**  
   **Requested** means: the browser called `request_lane_action` and the server set the lane to “waiting for the connector.” There is **no live data** until the connector **claims** the lane and the subprocess moves to **Running** and starts streaming updates.

So **Requested without ever seeing Running** means: **nothing on the bench is successfully doing `claim_lane` and starting the run** (connector not running, wrong ERP URL/API, station/Target PC mismatch, or claim failing).

### Why so many `request_lane_action` lines

Each time you click a mode / Step Sweep / Full Test, the client calls `request_lane_action`. On success it also does `frm.reload_doc()`. Rapid clicks or repeated tries produce many of those lines. That is expected if you are clicking a lot.

### `socketio_client.js: throttled`

That comes from **Frappe’s** Socket.IO client when many events fire in a short time. It is a rate limit, not a bug in your PTS3 script. You can ignore it unless the whole UI feels broken.

### What to fix in practice

1. **Keep `pts3_connector.py` running** on the Prerana PC while you use the form, and confirm it can reach `ERP=http://...` and that **Target PC** on the doc matches the station name the connector uses (`Prerana` / hostname / `PTS3_TARGET_PC`).

2. **Fix `PTS3_VISA_RESOURCE`** (or `PTS3_VISA_RESOURCE.txt`) so the run does not fail immediately after **Running**; otherwise you will keep cycling **Failed** → click → **Requested**.

3. If status stays **Requested** for tens of seconds, check the **connector terminal** for errors and that it logs something like **Claimed** / **launching** for that document and lane.

In short: **Requested + zero live lengths** = waiting for the connector; **Failed** = run started but the bench reported failure; **throttled** = normal under heavy UI traffic.

# PTS3 Server API – Summary

## Files created/updated

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `pts3_api_server_script.py` | Server script with all 10 endpoints |
| `21_PTS3_API_DEPLOYMENT_AND_TESTS.md` | Deployment steps and test calls |

---

## Endpoints implemented

| # | api_cmd | Behavior |
|---|---------|----------|
| 1 | **request_lane_action** | Rejects blank `pcb_serial_no` → `reason: "pcb_serial_no_required"`; sets `lane_action`, `lane_action_status = "Requested"`; does not create `run_id` |
| 2 | **request_abort** | Sets `abort_requested = 1` on lane |
| 3 | **claim_lane** | Only creates `run_id`; succeeds only if status is `Requested` |
| 4 | **update_lane_fields** | Verifies `run_id`; updates allowed live/heartbeat fields |
| 5 | **append_lane_log** | Appends `log_chunk` to `lane_log`; verifies `run_id` |
| 6 | **save_final_result** | Rejects duplicate `run_id`; creates PTS3 Result; updates `latest_result_id` and summary fields on lane |
| 7 | **mark_lane_failed** | Sets `Failed`, `error_message`, clears `abort_requested` |
| 8 | **abort_lane** | Sets `Aborted`, clears `abort_requested` |
| 9 | **reset_lane** | Clears action, status, live fields, logs; keeps `pcb_serial_no`, `latest_result_id` |
| 10 | **get_status_snapshot** | Returns full doc and lanes for UI |

---

## Requirements coverage

- Uses actual field names from the created doctypes
- `request_lane_action` rejects blank `pcb_serial_no`
- `claim_lane` is the only place that creates `run_id`
- `save_final_result` rejects duplicate `run_id` and updates `latest_result_id` on the lane
- `lane_action` uses internal codes: `step_sweep`, `mode1`, `mode2`, `mode3`, `mode0`, `full_test`
- RestrictedPython-safe (no f-strings, no `.format()`)

---

## Deployment

1. Setup → Server Script → New  
2. Script Type: **API**  
3. API Method: **pts3_api**  
4. Paste the contents of `pts3_api_server_script.py`  
5. Save  

---

## Test calls (bench console)

```python
# Create test doc
doc = frappe.new_doc("PTS3 Test")
doc.target_pc = "PTS3-PC-01"
doc.append("lanes", {"lane_no": 1, "pcb_serial_no": "TEST001"})
doc.insert()
frappe.db.commit()
docname = doc.name

# request_lane_action
frappe.call("pts3_api", api_cmd="request_lane_action", docname=docname, lane_no=1, action="step_sweep")

# claim_lane
r = frappe.call("pts3_api", api_cmd="claim_lane", docname=docname, lane_no=1, connector_name="CONN-01")
run_id = r.get("message", {}).get("run_id")

# save_final_result
frappe.call("pts3_api", api_cmd="save_final_result", docname=docname, lane_no=1, run_id=run_id,
    result={"run_id": run_id, "serial": "TEST001", "operation": "step_sweep", "datetime": frappe.utils.now(),
            "left_right_diff_summary": {"metadata": {"status": "Pass"}}})
```

## Problem

- **`target_pc`** on **PTS3 Test** was **`hidden=1`** in the DocType definition, and the client script also treated it like a hidden operator field.
- A **custom HTML “Station” input** tried to drive **`target_pc`** via **`frm.set_value`**. In Frappe, **setting hidden fields from the client is unreliable**, so **Station / Target PC** edits did not persist for **`PTS3-TEST-00001`**.
- **DocType defaults** only affect **new** documents, not existing ones.

---

## Code to change (primary fix)

**File:** `PTS3_Test_Client_Script.js`  
Paths (keep in sync if you maintain both):

- `PCB_IQC_ERPNext_Project/EXAMPLES/CHARGPT  TRIAL/PTS3 test/PTS3_Test_Client_Script.js`
- `.../PTS3 test/PTS3 test/PTS3_Test_Client_Script.js`

**Changes:**

1. **`hide_operator_fields`** — Do **not** hide **`target_pc`**. Force it **visible** and **editable**:

```79:95:c:\Users\pc\Desktop\PCB_IQC_ERPNext_Project\EXAMPLES\CHARGPT  TRIAL\PTS3 test\PTS3_Test_Client_Script.js
  function hide_operator_fields(frm) {
    var hidden = ["naming_series", "name_serial_slug", "name_op_short", "test_status", "station_name", "operator", "remarks"];
    hidden.forEach(function (fn) {
      if (frm.fields_dict[fn]) {
        frm.set_df_property(fn, "hidden", 1);
      }
    });
    // target_pc must stay visible (or at least not hidden): hidden Data fields often reject
    // frm.set_value in the browser, so the Station box could not update the document.
    if (frm.fields_dict.target_pc) {
      frm.set_df_property("target_pc", "hidden", 0);
      frm.set_df_property("target_pc", "read_only", 0);
    }
    if (frm.fields_dict.lanes) {
      frm.set_df_property("lanes", "hidden", 1);
    }
  }
```

2. **Lane dashboard HTML** — Remove the fake **Station** `<input>` and any **click/save handlers** that called **`frm.set_value("target_pc", …)`**. Replace with a short hint to edit **Target PC** on the main form and **Save**:

```390:393:c:\Users\pc\Desktop\PCB_IQC_ERPNext_Project\EXAMPLES\CHARGPT  TRIAL\PTS3 test\PTS3_Test_Client_Script.js
    html += '<div class="pts3-header-right">';

    html += "</div></div>";
```

### What went wrong (Frappe **14.99**)

`Page.load_assets()` does this:

1. Sets `self.script = ""`
2. Builds `path = …/frappe/core/page/pts3_book`
3. Loads `pts3_book.js` **from disk** if present  
4. Then runs **`os.listdir(path)`** with **no** `os.path.exists(path)` check  

So if the **`pts3_book` folder was missing**, you get exactly:

`FileNotFoundError: ... 'apps/frappe/frappe/core/page/pts3_book'`

Having JS only in the **Page** document in the DB is **not enough** on Frappe 14 for this flow.

---

### What we changed

1. **`INSTALL_PTS3_BOOK_AND_API_VIA_AUTO_EXECUTOR.py`**  
   Writes the JS using **`frappe.get_app_path("frappe")`** →  
   `.../frappe/frappe/core/page/pts3_book/pts3_book.js` (reliable absolute path).

2. **`EXAMPLES/.../pts3_bench_install.py`**  
   Same disk write logic.

3. **`PATCH_PTS3_BOOK_F14_DISK.py`** (new)  
   Only fixes the **disk file + Page** for sites that were installed before this fix.

4. **Ran the patch on your stack** — it succeeded:

```text
Wrote: /home/frappe/frappe-bench/apps/frappe/frappe/core/page/pts3_book/pts3_book.js
OK: Page pts3-book fixed for Frappe 14 load_assets
```

---

2. Open **`/app/pts3-book`** again (or the Home shortcut).

`python PATCH_PTS3_BOOK_F14_DISK.py`  

or re-run the full installer.

Here’s what was going wrong and what we changed.

### Why you still saw “No sweep data” with `ok=True`

On **PTS3 Result**, if the DocType does **not** define **`final_graph_json`**, **`left_right_diff_summary_json`**, **`mode_values_json`**, **`raw_result_json`**, Frappe **does not store** those values. The row is still inserted, so the API can return **`ok=True`** and a **`result_id`**, but the JSON columns are empty → UI shows **No sweep data**.

### What we changed in `pts3_api_server_script.py`

1. **`pts3_result_missing_json_fieldnames()`** – Checks that those four fields exist on **PTS3 Result** before insert.
2. **If any are missing** – **`save_final_result`** now returns **`ok: False`**, **`reason: pts3_result_doctype_missing_fields`**, and **`missing_fields: [...]`** so this is visible (no more false “success”).
3. **If all are present** – After **`res.insert()`**, the script also runs **`frappe.db.set_value`** on the same four JSON fields so values are written again at the DB layer (helps if anything odd happened on `insert()`).
4. **Bugfix** – Lane “Done” / **`latest_result_id`** updates only run when the insert actually succeeds (not when the DocType check fails).

### What you should do on the ERP server

1. **Add the fields** (or run `fix_pts3_result_json_fields.py` from bench console), then:
   - `bench --site <site> migrate`
   - `bench --site <site> clear-cache`
2. **Paste the updated `pts3_api`** script into Frappe and save.
3. **Run a new test.**  
   - If fields are still missing, the connector will **fail** with something like  
     `pts3_result_doctype_missing_fields` and a list of **`missing_fields`** (connector was updated to log that too).

After **`migrate`**, new results should show sweep data. Old rows like **`0j5najsd14`** were saved without JSON and will stay empty unless you re-run a test or backfill manually.

## Recommended final architecture
- **`pts3_runner_daemon.py`** (new): long-running localhost TCP worker
  - initializes PyVISA + scope once
  - keeps scope session alive
  - streams the **same JSON event types** (`status`, `sweep_point`, `mode_complete`, `log`, `completed`, `failed`)
- **`pts3_connector.py`** (updated):
  - **tries runner first**
  - **falls back to subprocess** (`AUTO_PTS3v17.py --cli`) if runner isn’t reachable
  - abort requests send a runner `abort` command when using runner

- **Added** `c:\Users\pc\Desktop\PCB_IQC_ERPNext_Project\EXAMPLES\CHARGPT  TRIAL\PTS3 test\pts3_runner_daemon.py`
- **Updated** `c:\Users\pc\Desktop\PCB_IQC_ERPNext_Project\EXAMPLES\CHARGPT  TRIAL\PTS3 test\pts3_connector.py`
- **Added** `c:\Users\pc\Desktop\PCB_IQC_ERPNext_Project\EXAMPLES\CHARGPT  TRIAL\PTS3 test\PTS3_RUNNER_README.md`

## Updated connector flow
- Claim lane → `run_id`
- **Try connect** `127.0.0.1:8765` and send:
  - `{"cmd":"step_sweep"/"mode1"...,"serial":...,"lane_no":...,"run_id":...}`
- Read newline-delimited JSON events exactly like stdout parsing
- If connect fails → spawn `AUTO_PTS3v17.py --cli` as before

## Worker startup instructions
See `PTS3_RUNNER_README.md`. Minimal:

```bash
python pts3_runner_daemon.py
```

## Failure / reconnect strategy
- Runner keeps a single scope instance.
- On `read_all()` failure: **one reconnect attempt**, then retry once.
- If scope is unplugged: next command will reconnect.

1. Start `pts3_runner_daemon.py` on station PC.
2. Start `pts3_connector.py` normally.
3. Confirm connector log shows: `Using runner 127.0.0.1:8765`

### AI  ``

### What’s happening now (why you see `duplicate_run_id`)
Right now the PTS3 API is written in a **“one-run-per-record”** style:

- `claim_lane` generates a `run_id`
- `save_final_result` **creates a new `PTS3 Result`**
- if you call `save_final_result` again with the **same** `run_id` (Mode1/2/3/0 after Sweep), the API **rejects it** as `duplicate_run_id`

That’s exactly the error in your screenshot: the test runs, but the server refuses to store the second result because it thinks it’s a duplicate run.

### The approach that matches how you work (recommended)
Switch to a **“session upsert”** model:

- **One `run_id` per serial session**
- Step Sweep + Mode1 + Mode2 + Mode3 + Mode0 all **save into the same `PTS3 Result` row**
- Each save **merges** the JSON:
  - Sweep updates: `final_graph_json` + `left_right_diff_summary_json`
  - Mode updates: **merge into** `mode_values_json` (adds/overwrites `Mode1`, `Mode2`, `Mode3`, `Mode0`)
  - Raw result: merged into `raw_result_json`

This exactly matches your Excel “single row per serial session” view, but stored reliably in JSON.

### I implemented this now (server-side)
I updated **both copies** of the server API script:

- `.../PTS3 test/pts3_api_server_script.py`
- `.../PTS3 test/PTS3 test/pts3_api_server_script.py`

Changes included:

- **`request_lane_action`**: no longer clears `run_id` every time; it keeps it for the same serial (but clears it if the serial changed).
- **`claim_lane`**: reuses existing `run_id` if present; only generates a new one if blank.
- **`save_final_result`**: no longer rejects duplicate `run_id`; it **updates/merges into the existing `PTS3 Result`**.

### What you need to do to activate it on ERPNext
1. Open **Server Script** in ERPNext (your `pts3_api`).
2. Paste the updated script content (from whichever file you treat as source-of-truth).
3. Save.
4. Run: `bench --site <yoursite> clear-cache` (or clear cache from UI).
5. Re-run: Step Sweep → Mode1 → Mode2 → Mode3 → Mode0  
   **Expected:** No duplicate error; the same `PTS3 Result` gets updated/filled.

### Small note about “one record”
Your `PTS3 Result.name` naming (`pts3_<serial>_sweep_1` etc.) is still fine: the record name comes from the **first save** in that session (usually sweep). Later mode saves will **update that same record**.

If you want the *name* to be session-only (not sweep/mode), tell me your preferred naming (e.g. `pts3_<serial>_<session>`) and I’ll adjust the allocator.
