Here’s a concise diagnosis and what was changed.

## What was going wrong (not “wrong doctype”)

The connector **is** sending the full compiled payload: your log shows `graph.type=sweep`, `freqs=21`, L/R/D all 21, and `result_json length=2587`, and the API returned **`ok=True`** with **`result_id=u568ukafdf`**.

So the problem was almost certainly **on the server side when building the `PTS3 Result` row**, not “uploading to the wrong DocType”:

1. **Loose validation** – `save_final_result` treated a non-empty `left_right_diff_summary` as valid if the dict had **any** keys (e.g. only `metadata`). The UI needs either a **sweep `graph`** with `freqs`, or **non-empty `left` / `right` / `diff` maps**. Metadata-only is not enough → you could get **`ok=True`** but empty sweep sections.

2. **REST / nested JSON** – Nested `result` can be flattened or stringified. The script already merges **`result_json`**; that merge is now **stronger** and **`len(parsed) > 0` was removed** so an empty `{}` parse doesn’t block merging.

3. **F12 looked empty** – Logging used **`console.debug`**, which is often **hidden** unless “Verbose” is enabled. It’s now **`console.info`** with the `[PTS3]` prefix so default console levels show it.

4. **Rare case** – If **`final_graph_json` / `left_right_diff_summary_json`** are not readable for the user’s role, the form can show **length 0** in `[PTS3]` logs even when the DB has data. Worth checking **Role Permissions → PTS3 Result → read** on those Code fields.

## What we changed in the repo

- **`pts3_api_server_script.py`**:  
  - Merge from **`result_json`** again into `r`, normalize **string** `graph` / table.  
  - **`_fill_lrd_from_sweep_graph`** so sweep arrays always become L/R/D maps when maps are empty.  
  - For **`operation == step_sweep`**, reject with **`sweep_payload_missing`** if there is still no real sweep data (so you don’t get another silent empty Result).  
- **`PTS3_Test_Client_Script.js`** and **`pts3_result_client_script.js`**: **`pts3Dbg` → `console.info`**.

```javascript
    render_runs(data) {
      const me = this;
      const runs = data.runs || [];

      if (!runs.length && this.offset === 0) {
        this.$runs.html(
          '<p class="text-muted" style="margin-top:0.75rem;">' +
          __('No runs found for this PCB Serial No') +
          '</p>'
        );
        this.$table = null;
        this.$tbody = null;
        return;
      }

      // Create table once
      if (!this.$table) {
        this.$table = $(
          '<table class="table table-bordered table-condensed">' +
            '<thead><tr>' +
              '<th>' + __('Datetime') + '</th>' +
              '<th>' + __('Operation') + '</th>' +
              '<th>' + __('Pass/Fail') + '</th>' +
              '<th>' + __('Dominant') + '</th>' +
              '<th>' + __('Max') + '</th>' +
              '<th>' + __('Run ID') + '</th>' +
              '<th style="width: 120px;">' + __('Open') + '</th>' +
            '</tr></thead>' +
            '<tbody></tbody>' +
          '</table>'
        );
        this.$tbody = this.$table.find('tbody');
        this.$runs.empty().append(this.$table);
      }

      // If this is the first page, clear existing rows
      if (this.offset === 0) {
        this.$tbody.empty();
      }

      // Append rows
      runs.forEach(function (run) {
        const dt = run.datetime
          ? frappe.datetime.str_to_user(run.datetime)
          : '';

        const $tr = $('<tr></tr>');

        $tr.append(
          $('<td></td>').text(dt || '-'),
          $('<td></td>').text(run.operation || '-'),
          $('<td></td>').text(run.pass_fail || '-'),
          $('<td></td>').text(run.dominant_channel || '-'),
          $('<td></td>').text(
            (run.max_value !== undefined && run.max_value !== null)
              ? run.max_value
              : '-'
          ),
          $('<td></td>').text(run.run_id || run.name || '-')
        );

        const $btn = $('<button class="btn btn-xs btn-default"></button>')
          .text(__('Open Result'))
          .on('click', function () {
            if (run.name) {
              frappe.set_route('Form', 'PTS3 Result', run.name);
            }
          });

        $tr.append($('<td></td>').append($btn));

        me.$tbody.append($tr);
      });

      // Setup / update "Load more" button
      if (!this.$more_wrap) {
        this.$more_wrap = $(
          '<div class="text-center" style="margin-top:0.75rem;"></div>'
        );
        this.$more_btn = $(
          '<button class="btn btn-sm btn-default"></button>'
        ).appendTo(this.$more_wrap);

        this.$more_btn.on('click', function () {
          me.offset += me.limit;
          me.fetch_data();
        });

        this.$runs.append(this.$more_wrap);
      }

      const has_more = (data.has_more === true) || (runs.length >= this.limit);

      if (has_more) {
        this.$more_wrap.show();
        this.$more_btn
          .prop('disabled', false)
          .text(__('Load More'));
      } else {
        if (this.offset === 0) {
          // Single page only: hide button
          this.$more_wrap.hide();
        } else {
          // No further pages
          this.$more_wrap.show();
          this.$more_btn
            .prop('disabled', true)
            .text(__('No more runs'));
        }
      }
    }
```

Here’s what was going wrong and what we changed.

### 1. **PyVISA “access violation”**
NI‑VISA + **Python 3.13** + Tek USB is touchy. You were calling **`list_resources()` twice** before opening the scope:

1. At **import** in `AUTO_PTS3v17.py` (old code).
2. Again inside **`Scope_header_v2.Oscilloscope.__init__`** every time you created a scope.

That second enumeration often triggered the fault you saw in `_find_resources` / `open`.

**Changes:**
- **`AUTO_PTS3v17.py`**: No VISA scan at import. Added **`ensure_visa()`**, which creates one `ResourceManager`, runs **`list_resources()` once**, and sets `scope_res`. GUI/CLI call **`ensure_visa()`** before any scope use.
- **`Scope_header_v2.py`**: If **`rm`** and **`resource_name`** are both passed (normal PTS3 path), it **opens that resource only** and **does not** call **`list_resources()`** again.

Optional: set **`PTS3_VISA_RESOURCE=USB0::0x0699::0x03C4::C012223::INSTR`** (your address) so `ensure_visa()` **skips** `list_resources()` completely.

### 2. **“Playing: 0 Hz” in ERP**
Mode runs didn’t send a **`freq`** field on status events, so the dashboard kept **0 Hz** (sweep is the only path that used to set frequency).

**Change:** During mode capture, the CLI now emits status with **`"freq": 80`** while the 80 Hz tone is active, and **`"freq": 0`** when it stops, so the connector can push **`live_current_freq`** correctly.

### 3. **What you should deploy**
Copy the updated files to **`d:\PTS3_Modified\PTS3_Modified\`** (or your live folder):

- `AUTO_PTS3v17.py`
- `Scope_header_v2.py`

### 4. **If crashes continue**
- Prefer **Python 3.12.x** for PyVISA/NI‑VISA on Windows until stacks catch up with 3.13.  
- Install the latest **NI‑VISA** runtime and Tek **USB** driver.  
- Only one app should own the scope at a time (close Tek OpenChoice, etc.).

Your log still showed a valid **Mode0** line after the faults, so the hardware path works; reducing duplicate VISA calls should remove most of those fatal exceptions.

### AI  ``

That error is because **Frappe thinks `pts3-book` is a “Standard Page” that lives on disk**, so it tries to load assets from:

`apps/frappe/frappe/core/page/pts3_book`

…but that folder does **not** exist (because `pts3_book` is your custom page, not part of Frappe core).

### Fix (recommended, works on v14 without any app folder)
Make `pts3-book` a **Non‑Standard Page** stored in the database.

- Go to **Page List** → open **`pts3-book`**  
- Set:
  - **Standard** = **0 / unchecked**
  - **Module** = your module (e.g. **PCB IQC**) (not “Core”)
- Paste your **`pts3_book.js`** into the Page’s **Script** field (and any CSS into **Style**).
- Save
- Run **Clear Cache** (bench or UI), then reload `pts3-book`.

### Alternative fix (filesystem “standard page” way)
Only if you want it as code in an app:

Create the folder inside your custom app (not in `frappe`):

`apps/<your_app>/<your_app>/<your_app>/page/pts3_book/pts3_book.js`  
(and `pts3_book.py`, `pts3_book.json` if needed)

Then set the Page to **Standard=1** and Module = `<your_app>`.

If you tell me whether you want **DB page** (fast) or **app page** (code-managed), I’ll point you to the exact place to paste `pts3_book.js` you already have in this repo.

## Endpoints implemented

| # | api_cmd | Behavior |
|---|---------|----------|
| 1 | **request_lane_action** | Rejects blank `pcb_serial_no` → `reason: "pcb_serial_no_required"`; sets `lane_action`, `lane_action_status = "Requested"`; does not create `run_id` |

| 5 | **append_lane_log** | Appends `log_chunk` to `lane_log`; verifies `run_id` |

| 7 | **mark_lane_failed** | Sets `Failed`, `error_message`, clears `abort_requested` |
| 8 | **abort_lane** | Sets `Aborted`, clears `abort_requested` |
| 9 | **reset_lane** | Clears action, status, live fields, logs; keeps `pcb_serial_no`, `latest_result_id` |
| 10 | **get_status_snapshot** | Returns full doc and lanes for UI |

Here’s what’s wrong and what to change, in plain language.

## What’s wrong

- `opv` is only set **inside** `if existing:` (when you’re **updating** an existing **PTS3 Result**).
- After that, the script always runs the block that starts with **“Do NOT overwrite sweep JSON…”** and uses **`if opv == "step_sweep"`**.
- When there is **no** existing result yet (`else:` → **new** PTS3 Result), the script **never** sets `opv`, so Python raises **`NameError: name 'opv' is not defined`**.

So the bug is: **`opv` must exist for both “update existing” and “create new”.**

---

## What to do (one fix)

**1. Add this *before* `if existing:`** (right after the `ap_str` block, same indent as `if existing:`):

```python
                        opv = (operation or "").strip()
```

**2. Delete the old line inside `if existing:`** that only says:

```python
                            opv = (operation or "").strip()
```

(so you don’t set `opv` twice).

After the change it should look like:

```text
                        ... ap_str handling ends ...

                        opv = (operation or "").strip()
                        if existing:
                            d = frappe.get_doc("PTS3 Result", existing)
                            if opv == "step_sweep" or opv == "submit":
                                ...
```

**3.** Save the Server Script, then run **`bench clear-cache`** (or your site’s equivalent).

**4. (Optional)** Change `PTS3_API_VERSION` (e.g. to `v3`) so you can see in API responses that the new script is live.

That’s the only change required for this **`opv`** error; everything else in your script can stay as-is.

### AI  ``

Here’s what was implemented and how to deploy it.

### Name pattern

New **PTS3 Result** rows get names like:

- `pts3_<serial_slug>_sweep_<n>` — for **`step_sweep`** and **`submit`**
- `pts3_<serial_slug>_mode_<n>` — for **`mode1`**, **`mode2`**, **`mode3`**, **`mode0`**, **`full_test`**

`<serial_slug>` comes from PCB serial (letters, digits, `_`, `-` only; other characters become `_`; max 80 chars; empty → `UNKNOWN`).

`<n>` is a **per-(serial, sweep|mode)** counter: it looks at existing `tabPTS3 Result` names with the same prefix and uses **max + 1** (with a small retry loop if there’s a clash).

### AI  ``

## Yes — this client script had a real issue

### What I found
In `pts3_result_client_script.js`, `safe_json(val, null)` was **never returning `null`** on bad JSON / empty string.  
Because it used `fallback || {}`, passing `null` still became `{}`.

That causes **silent “missing charts” behavior**:
- `render_step_sweep()` tries to parse `final_graph_json` and `left_right_diff_summary_json`.
  - If parsing fails (or field is empty), it becomes `{}` and you end up with **“No sweep data”** even though you expected it to fall back properly.
- `render_mode()` would also get `{}` and then render an **empty Mode section** (no chart + no “No mode data” message).

### Fix applied
I patched `pts3_result_client_script.js` to:
- **Make `safe_json` respect an explicit fallback (even `null`)** instead of forcing `{}`.
- **Make `render_mode` show “No mode data”** when the parsed object is empty.

These changes are now in:

- `PCB_IQC_ERPNext_Project/EXAMPLES/CHARGPT  TRIAL/PTS3 test/pts3_result_client_script.js`

### Why this matters for your charts
After the server-side fix (don’t wipe sweep JSON on mode saves) + this client-side fix (don’t silently convert bad/empty JSON into `{}`), your PTS3 Result page will correctly build:
- **Step sweep chart** from `final_graph_json` (or fallback from `left_right_diff_summary_json`)
- **Diff vs Hz chart** from the same sweep data
- **Mode chart** from `mode_values_json`

If you want, paste one actual `final_graph_json` value from a failing record (first ~200 chars is enough) and I’ll confirm it’s valid JSON and matches what the renderer expects.

### AI  ``

Identifying the issue: the connector warms the runner (scope stays open), then mode jobs run `AUTO_PTS3v17.py --cli` in a subprocess that calls `list_resources()` and `open_resource()` — a second open of the same USB device while the runner holds it, causing NI-VISA access violations on Python 3.13.

Implementing: (1) make runner warmup opt-in so we don't hold the scope by default when modes use subprocess; (2) inject `PTS3_VISA_RESOURCE` into the connector process after successful warmup so CLI skips `list_resources`; (3) warn when `list_resources` is about to run without `PTS3_VISA_RESOURCE`.

I found the real issue.

## Why nothing is showing

Your `PTS3 Result` client script is rendering the HTML field the wrong way.

Right now it does this:

* checks `frm.fields_dict.result_inspection`
* then sets:

  * `frm.doc.result_inspection = render_inspection(frm);`
  * `frm.refresh_field("result_inspection");` 

That pattern works for normal data fields, but **HTML fields in Frappe are not rendered by writing into `frm.doc.<fieldname>`**.

For an HTML field, you should render into the field wrapper, like:

```javascript
frm.get_field("result_inspection").$wrapper.html(render_inspection(frm));
```

Because of that, your field exists, the layout is correct, the JSON is correct, but the HTML never actually gets injected into the visible field.

---

## What should be changed

In `pts3_result_client_script.js`, replace the refresh block with wrapper rendering.

### Current wrong logic

It is effectively doing this: 

```javascript
if (frm.fields_dict.result_inspection) {
  frm.doc.result_inspection = render_inspection(frm);
  frm.refresh_field("result_inspection");
}
```

### Correct logic

It should do this instead:

```javascript
refresh: function (frm) {
  var field = frm.get_field("result_inspection");
  if (field && field.$wrapper) {
    field.$wrapper.html(render_inspection(frm));
  }
}
```

---

     - `last_heartbeat_push` — reset every 5 s for `last_heartbeat_at` updates
   - Heartbeats are now sent to ERP every 5 seconds during runs.

2. **Subprocess stderr**
   - Switched from `stderr=subprocess.PIPE` to `stderr=subprocess.STDOUT`.
   - stderr is merged into stdout; non-JSON lines (including stderr) go to `lane_log`.
   - Avoids pipe blocking when the worker writes a lot to stderr.

3. **Post-process completion/failure**
   - Added `failure_marked` flag.
   - All `api_mark_lane_failed` paths now:
     - Check `not failure_marked` (and `not completed_received` where needed)
     - Set `failure_marked = True` before calling the API
   - Prevents double failure marking after completed, failed, aborted, or launch-failure.

### Files Updated

- **`pts3_connector.py`** — All hardening changes
- **`23_CONNECTOR_DEPLOYMENT_AND_TESTS.md`** — Smoke test steps, heartbeat check, abort limitation note
- **`24_CONNECTOR_HARDENING_REPORT.md`** — New report with fixes, limitations, and smoke test steps

### Remaining Limitations

| Limitation | Notes |
|------------|-------|
| Abort is line-driven | Checked only when stdout lines arrive; can lag during long silent captures (e.g. 5 s mode). Documented; acceptable for v1. |
| stderr merged with stdout | stderr and stdout both go to `lane_log`; cannot distinguish them. |

7. Verify no double-fail (`mark_lane_failed` called at most once per run).

## 1. What “required output” actually is

1. **Stimulus path:** PC audio (or line-out) actually drives the **headphone / jig** input the PCB expects; volume up; correct output device (not a muted Bluetooth sink if you expect analog).
2. **Scope probes:** **CH1 / CH2** on the **correct** BCR/BCL (or your defined) points; **ground** on board/jig ground.
3. **PCB mode:** For each step (Mode 1, 2, 3, 0), the board is in the **intended mode** before/during capture (your procedure).
4. **Scope front panel:** If trace is still flat after software config, use **Autoset** once, then adjust **trigger level** on the channel that has signal.

|--------|------|

| **`AUTO_PTS3v17.py`** (updated) | Mode capture + step sweep call those configures |

### AI  ``

Here’s what was going wrong and what we changed.

## Cause of the access violations

1. **`list_resources()`** — With **`PTS3_VISA_RESOURCE` unset**, `ensure_visa()` enumerates devices. On **Python 3.13 + NI-VISA** that often triggers **access violations** (as in your stack trace).

2. **Double use of the same USB scope** — The connector **warmed the runner**, so **`pts3_runner_daemon` kept the scope open**. Mode jobs then run **`AUTO_PTS3v17.py --cli`** in a **new process**, which **opens the same USB instrument again**. Two sessions on one USB resource is a bad idea and can produce **AVs in `open_resource` / `parse_resource_extended`**, even if a later attempt “connects.”

3. **Table vs log** — **`P1=632.31`** in the UI is usually the **averaged / saved** result; the last **`[Scope]`** line can be a **single sample** at the end (**820 mV**), so they don’t have to match exactly.

## Code updates (in your Desktop project copies)

| Change | Purpose |
|--------|--------|
| **`PTS3_RUNNER_WARMUP=1` required** for startup warmup | Default is **no** runner warmup, so the runner does **not** hold the scope while **subprocess** mode jobs run (avoids double-open). |
| After a **successful** warmup, set **`PTS3_VISA_RESOURCE`** in the connector process | Child **`--cli`** runs inherit it and **skip** `list_resources()`. |
| **`ensure_visa()`** | Logs a **warning** before `list_resources()` if **`PTS3_VISA_RESOURCE`** is not set. |

**Always** set the scope address (use your real string):

```powershell
$env:PTS3_VISA_RESOURCE = "USB0::0x0699::0x03C4::C012223::INSTR"
```

Then start the connector (or use **setx** / system environment for a permanent setting).

- **Do not** set **`PTS3_RUNNER_WARMUP=1`** unless you know you need the runner to hold the scope **and** you’re not using **subprocess** mode jobs that open VISA again—or you’ll risk the same double-open issue.

With **`PTS3_VISA_RESOURCE`** set and **default warmup off**, each mode job should do a **single** `open_resource` on that string and **avoid** `list_resources()`, which should remove most of the AV noise and stabilize the run.

Here’s what was going wrong:

**Cause:** In Frappe **Server Scripts**, code runs under **RestrictedPython**. Tuple assignment like `graph, table = fill_lrd_from_sweep_graph(...)` is compiled in a way that needs **`_unpack_sequence_`**, which is **not** provided in that environment → **`NameError: name '_unpack_sequence_' is not defined`**.

**Change:** Drop tuple unpacking and use a single return value + indexing:

```python
lrd_out = fill_lrd_from_sweep_graph(r, graph, table)
graph = lrd_out[0]
table = lrd_out[1]
```

(and the same pattern for the second call with `lrd_out2`).

**In the repo:** `pts3_api_server_script.py` is updated and a short comment was added at the top: **no** `a, b = func()` in Server Scripts.

**What you should do:** Paste the updated `pts3_api_server_script.py` into the Server Script **pts3_api** in Frappe and save, then run again.

If anything else blows up, the next place to check is other unpacks (e.g. `for k, v in ...`); we can rewrite those if needed.

Identifying the issue: the connector warms the runner (scope stays open), then mode jobs run `AUTO_PTS3v17.py --cli` in a subprocess that calls `list_resources()` and `open_resource()` — a second open of the same USB device while the runner holds it, causing NI-VISA access violations on Python 3.13.

Implementing: (1) make runner warmup opt-in so we don't hold the scope by default when modes use subprocess; (2) inject `PTS3_VISA_RESOURCE` into the connector process after successful warmup so CLI skips `list_resources`; (3) warn when `list_resources` is about to run without `PTS3_VISA_RESOURCE`.

### What’s happening now (why you see `duplicate_run_id`)
Right now the PTS3 API is written in a **“one-run-per-record”** style:

- `claim_lane` generates a `run_id`
- `save_final_result` **creates a new `PTS3 Result`**
- if you call `save_final_result` again with the **same** `run_id` (Mode1/2/3/0 after Sweep), the API **rejects it** as `duplicate_run_id`

That’s exactly the error in your screenshot: the test runs, but the server refuses to store the second result because it thinks it’s a duplicate run.

### The approach that matches how you work (recommended)
Switch to a **“session upsert”** model:

- **One `run_id` per serial session**
- Step Sweep + Mode1 + Mode2 + Mode3 + Mode0 all **save into the same `PTS3 Result` row**
- Each save **merges** the JSON:
  - Sweep updates: `final_graph_json` + `left_right_diff_summary_json`
  - Mode updates: **merge into** `mode_values_json` (adds/overwrites `Mode1`, `Mode2`, `Mode3`, `Mode0`)
  - Raw result: merged into `raw_result_json`

This exactly matches your Excel “single row per serial session” view, but stored reliably in JSON.

### I implemented this now (server-side)
I updated **both copies** of the server API script:

- `.../PTS3 test/pts3_api_server_script.py`
- `.../PTS3 test/PTS3 test/pts3_api_server_script.py`

Changes included:

- **`request_lane_action`**: no longer clears `run_id` every time; it keeps it for the same serial (but clears it if the serial changed).
- **`claim_lane`**: reuses existing `run_id` if present; only generates a new one if blank.
- **`save_final_result`**: no longer rejects duplicate `run_id`; it **updates/merges into the existing `PTS3 Result`**.

### What you need to do to activate it on ERPNext
1. Open **Server Script** in ERPNext (your `pts3_api`).
2. Paste the updated script content (from whichever file you treat as source-of-truth).
3. Save.
4. Run: `bench --site <yoursite> clear-cache` (or clear cache from UI).
5. Re-run: Step Sweep → Mode1 → Mode2 → Mode3 → Mode0  
   **Expected:** No duplicate error; the same `PTS3 Result` gets updated/filled.

### Small note about “one record”
Your `PTS3 Result.name` naming (`pts3_<serial>_sweep_1` etc.) is still fine: the record name comes from the **first save** in that session (usually sweep). Later mode saves will **update that same record**.

If you want the *name* to be session-only (not sweep/mode), tell me your preferred naming (e.g. `pts3_<serial>_<session>`) and I’ll adjust the allocator.

Here’s a concise diagnosis and what was changed.

## What was going wrong (not “wrong doctype”)

The connector **is** sending the full compiled payload: your log shows `graph.type=sweep`, `freqs=21`, L/R/D all 21, and `result_json length=2587`, and the API returned **`ok=True`** with **`result_id=u568ukafdf`**.

So the problem was almost certainly **on the server side when building the `PTS3 Result` row**, not “uploading to the wrong DocType”:

1. **Loose validation** – `save_final_result` treated a non-empty `left_right_diff_summary` as valid if the dict had **any** keys (e.g. only `metadata`). The UI needs either a **sweep `graph`** with `freqs`, or **non-empty `left` / `right` / `diff` maps**. Metadata-only is not enough → you could get **`ok=True`** but empty sweep sections.

2. **REST / nested JSON** – Nested `result` can be flattened or stringified. The script already merges **`result_json`**; that merge is now **stronger** and **`len(parsed) > 0` was removed** so an empty `{}` parse doesn’t block merging.

3. **F12 looked empty** – Logging used **`console.debug`**, which is often **hidden** unless “Verbose” is enabled. It’s now **`console.info`** with the `[PTS3]` prefix so default console levels show it.

4. **Rare case** – If **`final_graph_json` / `left_right_diff_summary_json`** are not readable for the user’s role, the form can show **length 0** in `[PTS3]` logs even when the DB has data. Worth checking **Role Permissions → PTS3 Result → read** on those Code fields.

## What we changed in the repo

- **`pts3_api_server_script.py`**:  
  - Merge from **`result_json`** again into `r`, normalize **string** `graph` / table.  
  - **`_fill_lrd_from_sweep_graph`** so sweep arrays always become L/R/D maps when maps are empty.  
  - For **`operation == step_sweep`**, reject with **`sweep_payload_missing`** if there is still no real sweep data (so you don’t get another silent empty Result).  
- **`PTS3_Test_Client_Script.js`** and **`pts3_result_client_script.js`**: **`pts3Dbg` → `console.info`**.

2. **Push** the updated client scripts for **PTS3 Test** and **PTS3 Result**.

3. Run a **new** test (or a new lane run). The old doc **`u568ukafdf`** was already saved with empty graph/LRD JSON; **this fix does not rewrite old rows**.

After deploy, open **PTS3 Result** and check the console for **`[PTS3] ... final_graph_json len=`** — if lengths are still **0**, focus on **permissions** or confirm the live **`pts3_api`** script actually contains the new helpers (`_merge_result_json_into_r`, `_sweep_payload_present`).

Here’s what that error means and how to fix it.

## What it means

**`SyntaxError: Unexpected token ')'`** is thrown while Frappe is **parsing your Client Script** JavaScript. Something in the text saved in **Customize → PTS3 Test → Client Script** is invalid—usually an **extra `)`**, a **missing `{` / `}`**, or a **bad partial paste** when you only changed `hide_operator_fields`.

The copy on disk is fine: `node --check` on  
`PCB_IQC_ERPNext_Project\EXAMPLES\CHARGPT  TRIAL\PTS3 test\PTS3_Test_Client_Script.js` **passes**, so the problem is almost certainly **what’s stored in ERPNext**, not that file as committed.

## Typical mistakes when replacing one function

- Leaving **two closing braces** for one function, or **dropping** the opening `function hide_operator_fields(frm) {`.
- Duplicating a line like **`});`** so you get `}););` or an extra `)`.
- Pasting **smart quotes** (`'` `'`) from Word/email instead of straight quotes (`'`).
- Accidentally **deleting** part of `frappe.ui.form.on("PTS3 Test", { ... });` above/below the edited block.

## What to do

1. Open **`PTS3_Test_Client_Script.js`** from your project (the full file, all **866** lines through the final `})();`).
2. In ERPNext, open the **PTS3 Test** Client Script editor, **select all**, **delete**, then **paste the entire file** (do not paste only `hide_operator_fields`).
3. **Save** the Client Script, then **hard refresh** the form (Ctrl+F5) or clear cache if you use it.

If it still errors, check **Form → there is only one Client Script** for PTS3 Test, or disable other scripts on that DocType temporarily.

## Quick local check before pasting

From PowerShell (optional):

```powershell
node --check "c:\Users\pc\Desktop\PCB_IQC_ERPNext_Project\EXAMPLES\CHARGPT  TRIAL\PTS3 test\PTS3_Test_Client_Script.js"
```

Exit code **0** means the file is valid JS; use that exact content in ERPNext.

## Why you might see no data

### 1. Station name mismatch

**Station** in PTS3 Test must match the connector’s PC name exactly.

On connector startup you’ll see something like:
```
[PTS3] Station field in PTS3 Test must exactly match: DESKTOP-AKC688N
```

Use that exact value in the Station field (e.g. `DESKTOP-AKC688N` or `PC-DESKTOP-AKC688N`).

### 2. Connector not finding the job

If you never see `Found 1 requested job(s)` or `Claimed...`:

- Station does not match the connector PC name.
- API key lacks read permission on PTS3 Test.

### 3. AUTO_PTS3 needs hardware

Step sweep uses:

- A `Step_sweep` folder with WAV files (40, 42, …, 80 Hz).
- VISA/Oscilloscope hardware.

Without these, the script may fail or emit no sweep data.

---

## What to do next

1. Restart the connector and note the exact PC name printed.
2. In PTS3 Test, set Station to that exact value.
3. Click Step Sweep and watch the connector terminal for:
   - `Found 1 requested job(s)`
   - `Claimed PTS3-TEST-00001 lane 1...`
4. If those appear but no sweep data, check that `Step_sweep` exists and VISA/scope are configured.

A troubleshooting guide is in `41_PTS3_CONNECTOR_NO_DATA_TROUBLESHOOTING.md`.

### What went wrong (Frappe **14.99**)

`Page.load_assets()` does this:

1. Sets `self.script = ""`
2. Builds `path = …/frappe/core/page/pts3_book`
3. Loads `pts3_book.js` **from disk** if present  
4. Then runs **`os.listdir(path)`** with **no** `os.path.exists(path)` check  

So if the **`pts3_book` folder was missing**, you get exactly:

`FileNotFoundError: ... 'apps/frappe/frappe/core/page/pts3_book'`

Having JS only in the **Page** document in the DB is **not enough** on Frappe 14 for this flow.

## What it means

**`SyntaxError: Unexpected token ')'`** is thrown while Frappe is **parsing your Client Script** JavaScript. Something in the text saved in **Customize → PTS3 Test → Client Script** is invalid—usually an **extra `)`**, a **missing `{` / `}`**, or a **bad partial paste** when you only changed `hide_operator_fields`.

## Typical mistakes when replacing one function

- Leaving **two closing braces** for one function, or **dropping** the opening `function hide_operator_fields(frm) {`.
- Duplicating a line like **`});`** so you get `}););` or an extra `)`.
- Pasting **smart quotes** (`'` `'`) from Word/email instead of straight quotes (`'`).
- Accidentally **deleting** part of `frappe.ui.form.on("PTS3 Test", { ... });` above/below the edited block.

### Run ID format updated (serial_test_series)

You were generating `run_id` like `docname|lane|random_hash`. I changed it so **new sessions** get a readable, stable `run_id`:

- **Format**: **`pts3run_<serial>_<testdoc>_<series>`**
- **Example**: **`pts3run_SUDESH_PTS3-TEST-00001_001`**

Where:
- `<serial>` is a safe slug of the PCB serial (letters/digits/`_`/`-`)
- `<testdoc>` is a slug of the PTS3 Test docname
- `<series>` is a **per-serial** increment based on how many `PTS3 Result` rows already exist for that serial

In both server script copies:
- `.../PTS3 test/pts3_api_server_script.py`
- `.../PTS3 test/PTS3 test/pts3_api_server_script.py`

Specifically inside **`claim_lane`**:
- If `run_id` is already present (session continuing), it keeps it.
- If blank (new session), it calls **`pts3_alloc_session_run_id()`** to create the new `run_id`.

## Problem

- **`target_pc`** on **PTS3 Test** was **`hidden=1`** in the DocType definition, and the client script also treated it like a hidden operator field.
- A **custom HTML “Station” input** tried to drive **`target_pc`** via **`frm.set_value`**. In Frappe, **setting hidden fields from the client is unreliable**, so **Station / Target PC** edits did not persist for **`PTS3-TEST-00001`**.
- **DocType defaults** only affect **new** documents, not existing ones.

---

## Code to change (primary fix)

**File:** `PTS3_Test_Client_Script.js`  
Paths (keep in sync if you maintain both):

- `PCB_IQC_ERPNext_Project/EXAMPLES/CHARGPT  TRIAL/PTS3 test/PTS3_Test_Client_Script.js`
- `.../PTS3 test/PTS3 test/PTS3_Test_Client_Script.js`

**Changes:**

1. **`hide_operator_fields`** — Do **not** hide **`target_pc`**. Force it **visible** and **editable**:

```79:95:c:\Users\pc\Desktop\PCB_IQC_ERPNext_Project\EXAMPLES\CHARGPT  TRIAL\PTS3 test\PTS3_Test_Client_Script.js
  function hide_operator_fields(frm) {
    var hidden = ["naming_series", "name_serial_slug", "name_op_short", "test_status", "station_name", "operator", "remarks"];
    hidden.forEach(function (fn) {
      if (frm.fields_dict[fn]) {
        frm.set_df_property(fn, "hidden", 1);
      }
    });
    // target_pc must stay visible (or at least not hidden): hidden Data fields often reject
    // frm.set_value in the browser, so the Station box could not update the document.
    if (frm.fields_dict.target_pc) {
      frm.set_df_property("target_pc", "hidden", 0);

      frm.set_df_property("lanes", "hidden", 1);
    }
  }
```

## 1) Make “running connector is enough” (auto-start daemon)
On the **test PC**, set this environment variable before starting the connector:

- **`PTS3_AUTO_START_RUNNER=1`**

## 2) Do you need to press “Save” to store into `PTS3 Result`?
**No.** Pressing **Save** on `PTS3 Test` only saves the test document UI fields.

`PTS3 Result` is created **automatically** when:
- the connector receives the CLI/runner event `type:"completed"`
- and the connector calls `pts3_api -> save_final_result`

If results are **not appearing automatically**, it’s usually because:
- the connector is failing `save_final_result` (it should set lane to **Failed** with `save_final_result failed: ...`), or
- the server script isn’t updated / rejected the payload.

## Connector Hardening Summary

### Fixes

1. **Heartbeat timing**
   - Replaced shared `last_heartbeat` with two timers:
     - `last_abort_check` — reset every 0.5 s for abort polling
     - `last_heartbeat_push` — reset every 5 s for `last_heartbeat_at` updates
   - Heartbeats are now sent to ERP every 5 seconds during runs.

2. **Subprocess stderr**
   - Switched from `stderr=subprocess.PIPE` to `stderr=subprocess.STDOUT`.
   - stderr is merged into stdout; non-JSON lines (including stderr) go to `lane_log`.
   - Avoids pipe blocking when the worker writes a lot to stderr.

3. **Post-process completion/failure**
   - Added `failure_marked` flag.
   - All `api_mark_lane_failed` paths now:
     - Check `not failure_marked` (and `not completed_received` where needed)
     - Set `failure_marked = True` before calling the API
   - Prevents double failure marking after completed, failed, aborted, or launch-failure.

| Limitation | Notes |

This is close, but I would make one correction pass before you wire the connector.

The API file covers the 10 endpoints you need and it correctly keeps claim_lane as the only creator of run_id, rejects blank pcb_serial_no in request_lane_action, verifies run_id for live updates, rejects duplicate run_id in save_final_result, and updates latest_result_id on the lane. The deployment/test guide also matches that behavior well.

What is good

request_lane_action does not generate run_id.

claim_lane owns run_id creation.

update_lane_fields limits writes to live/runtime fields only.

save_final_result creates PTS3 Result, maps the final payload cleanly, and sets lane summary fields.

get_status_snapshot gives the UI a compact lane snapshot for refresh.

What should be fixed before connector work
1. claim_lane should set lane_action_status = "Queued" first, then "Running" only when the worker actually starts

Right now claim_lane directly sets "Running".

That is workable, but not ideal. If the connector claims the lane and then fails before subprocess launch, ERP will show Running even though nothing started.

Better:

claim_lane → set Queued

connector starts subprocess successfully

connector calls update_lane_fields plus a status change endpoint, or claim_lane can optionally accept a second phase

then set Running

If you do not want a new endpoint, at minimum document that connector must call mark_lane_failed immediately if subprocess launch fails after claim.

2. request_lane_action should clear stale lane state

Currently it sets:

lane_action

lane_action_status = Requested

But it does not clear:

old run_id

old error_message

old live JSON

old progress fields

That can cause stale graph/table/status from previous runs to remain visible until the connector updates them.

So on new request, it should also clear the runtime/live fields, while keeping:

pcb_serial_no

latest_result_id

3. save_final_result should clear live runtime fields after success

Right now it sets:

lane_action_status = Done

latest_result_id

abort_requested = 0

summary fields

But it does not clear:

live_status

live_progress_message

last_heartbeat_at

You may want the final graph/table to remain, but at least:

live_status

live_progress_message
should be normalized to a final state, or cleared, so UI does not keep showing “Sweeping 78 Hz”.

4. save_final_result should validate required payload parts more strictly

Currently it only truly requires:

run_id

doc/lane match
and then it will create a result even if fields like left_right_diff_summary are weak or missing, because it falls back to {}.

Since your doctype made left_right_diff_summary_json mandatory, the API should also enforce:

operation

datetime

left_right_diff_summary

Otherwise the DB schema and API contract are not equally strict.

5. get_status_snapshot returning doc.as_dict() may be heavier than needed

It works, but for live UI refresh you probably only need:

doc-level status fields

lane array

Returning the full parent doc is okay for now, but later it may become noisy.

This is not a blocker, just an optimization note.

Here’s what was completed and how it maps to your workflow.

### 1. **`AUTO_PTS3v17.py`** (nested + synced parent copy)
- **`_cli_mode(..., play_80hz=True, external_stimulus_80hz=False)`**  
  - Default: same as before — start **80 Hz loop**, settle, **5 s** capture, then **stop**.  
  - **`full_test`** calls it with **`play_80hz=False`** when a single background loop is already running.
- **`_cli_full_test`**  
  - After **step sweep**, it starts **one** `Sine_80Hz.wav` **loop** (`SND_LOOP`), settles once, runs **Mode 1 → 2 → 3 → 0** **without** restarting the tone, then **`stop_wav()`** in a **`finally`**.

### 2. **`pts3_runner_daemon.py`** (long‑lived station worker; synced to parent folder)
This is what gives **“save serial → 80 Hz keeps playing while I run each mode”** when the connector uses the runner (not a one-shot subprocess per action):

- **`submit`** → starts **continuous 80 Hz** (same `SND_LOOP` pattern as AUTO), then emits **`completed`**.  
- **`step_sweep`** → **`_stop_80hz_continuous()`** at the start (so sweep WAVs are exclusive), then after **“Step sweep complete”** it **starts 80 Hz again** unless you set  
  **`PTS3_80HZ_AFTER_SWEEP=0`** (disables restart after sweep).  
- **`mode1`…`mode0`** → if 80 Hz isn’t already on, it starts it; **first** mode after a new arm uses **`MODE_80HZ_SETTLE_SEC`** (default **1.0 s**, override with **`PTS3_MODE_80HZ_SETTLE_SEC`**).  
- **`mode0`** **`completed`** → **`_stop_80hz_continuous()`** (tone stops after the last mode).  
- **`abort`** → also stops 80 Hz.

Paths: **`Sine_80Hz.wav`** next to the scripts, or **`PTS3_SINE80_FILE`** for a custom path.

### 3. **Important limitation (subprocess-only ERP path)**
If the connector **spawns a new `AUTO_PTS3v17.py --cli` process per button**, **Windows audio does not stay on** after that process exits, so **submit cannot leave 80 Hz running** for the **next** subprocess. For your **“save → tone stays on → Mode 1–0”** flow, run **`pts3_runner_daemon.py`** on the test PC (or **`PTS3_AUTO_START_RUNNER=1`** if you use that).

### Deploy
Copy to the station (next to the connector): updated **`AUTO_PTS3v17.py`**, **`pts3_runner_daemon.py`**, and **`Sine_80Hz.wav`**. Parent folder **`...\PTS3 test\`** is synced with **`...\PTS3 test\PTS3 test\`**.

Yes. **`pts3_runner_daemon.py` has to live on the test PC** — the same machine as the **connector** and the **USB scope**, because:

- It talks to the scope over **VISA on that PC**.
- The connector reaches it at **`127.0.0.1` (localhost)** — it is not something you run on the ERP server.

You don’t need it on the **ERPNext server**; only on each **PTS3 test station**.

**Ways to run it there**

1. **Manual** – start once per session:  
   `python pts3_runner_daemon.py` (from the folder that has `Scope_header_v2.py` and `Step_sweep`, etc.).

2. **Auto** – set env **`PTS3_AUTO_START_RUNNER=1`** for the connector so it tries to start the daemon if the port is free (still uses the same script path on that PC).

3. **Windows startup** – Task Scheduler or a shortcut in **Startup** that runs the same command.

If you **don’t** run the daemon, the connector falls back to spawning **`AUTO_PTS3v17.py`** each job (slower, full VISA init each time). The daemon is optional for correctness but **recommended** on the test PC for speed and stable scope use.

## Why you might see no data

### 1. Station name mismatch

**Station** in PTS3 Test must match the connector’s PC name exactly.

On connector startup you’ll see something like:
```
[PTS3] Station field in PTS3 Test must exactly match: DESKTOP-AKC688N
```

Use that exact value in the Station field (e.g. `DESKTOP-AKC688N` or `PC-DESKTOP-AKC688N`).

### 2. Connector not finding the job

If you never see `Found 1 requested job(s)` or `Claimed...`:

- Station does not match the connector PC name.
- API key lacks read permission on PTS3 Test.

### 3. AUTO_PTS3 needs hardware

Step sweep uses:

- A `Step_sweep` folder with WAV files (40, 42, …, 80 Hz).
- VISA/Oscilloscope hardware.

Without these, the script may fail or emit no sweep data.

---

## What to do next

1. Restart the connector and note the exact PC name printed.
2. In PTS3 Test, set Station to that exact value.
3. Click Step Sweep and watch the connector terminal for:
   - `Found 1 requested job(s)`
   - `Claimed PTS3-TEST-00001 lane 1...`
4. If those appear but no sweep data, check that `Step_sweep` exists and VISA/scope are configured.

A troubleshooting guide is in `41_PTS3_CONNECTOR_NO_DATA_TROUBLESHOOTING.md`.

### AI  ``

Here’s what the code actually does, and what usually breaks “like before.”

## 1. Two different things (easy to mix up)

| What you click | What it measures | “Fixed frequency” (40, 42, … 80 Hz)? |
|----------------|------------------|--------------------------------------|
| **Step Sweep** | One average **per frequency** → fills the **40hz … 80hz** columns + sweep graph | **Yes** — that’s the only path that does the **fixed-frequency grid** |
| **Mode 1 / 2 / 3 / 0** | **One** average over **5 seconds** (scope streaming) → **Mode1…Mode0** summary | **No** — modes are **not** “one reading per Hz”; they never were in `AUTO_PTS3v17.py` |

So: **readings at fixed frequencies** = **Step Sweep**, not the Mode buttons. Modes are **single averages per mode**, not a frequency table.

## 2. Typical “we used to get Hz readings” causes

1. **`Step_sweep` folder**  
   Step sweep (GUI and `--cli step_sweep`) needs a folder named **`Step_sweep`** next to **`AUTO_PTS3v17.py`**, with tone files whose names contain the Hz (e.g. `40 … 80`), same as before.  
   The connector runs with `cwd` = the folder that contains **`AUTO_PTS3v17.py`**. If that folder has **no** `Step_sweep` (or wrong files), you won’t get proper per-Hz sweep data.

2. **Audio**  
   Sweep plays WAVs with **`winsound`** (Windows). If volume is zero, wrong playback device, or files missing, the **stimulus** is wrong and scope readings won’t match what you expect.

3. **After ERP integration**  
   You might be looking only at **Mode** charts in ERP. Those show **Mode1…Mode0 bars**, not the **40–80 Hz** grid. The **Hz grid** comes from **Step Sweep** (`left`/`right`/`diff` vs frequency in the sweep graph/table).

## 3. Practical workflow (matches the Excel design)

1. **Submit** (init sheet)  
2. **Step Sweep** → fills **40–80 Hz** + sweep plot  
3. **Mode 1…0** → adds **mode** columns / `mode_values` (still not per-Hz)

## 4. If you need something else

If your old process was literally **“each mode at one chosen Hz”** (e.g. Mode 1 only at 60 Hz), that is **not** how `_cli_mode` works today — it doesn’t play a tone per mode. That would be a **new** behavior (extra option in the script + connector). Say what Hz per mode you need and we can sketch that change.

**Short answer:** For **fixed-frequency readings**, use **Step Sweep** and verify **`Step_sweep` WAVs + working directory + audio**. Mode buttons are **not** meant to replace that grid.

### AI  ``

Here’s what was going wrong and what we changed.

## What happened

1. **Mode 0 worked, then Mode 3 / 2 did nothing**  
   The log shows **`Windows fatal exception: access violation`** right after Mode 0. That **kills the Python process**. The next ERP actions start a **new** `AUTO_PTS3v17.py --cli` process. If the previous one died in the native VISA driver, the next run can fail or look like “no output.”

2. **Why it crashes (typical on your stack)**  
   - **Python 3.13 + NI-VISA + USB scope** is brittle.  
   - Each mode run **opens the scope → uses it → closes it**. The **next** job **reopens** USB **immediately**. That pattern often triggers **access violations** if the driver hasn’t finished releasing the device.

3. **DC coupling “by itself”**  
   That was from our script: we had defaulted to **DC** and sent coupling on **every** `configure()`. It wasn’t the scope randomly switching; it was **SCPI**.

---

## Fixes applied (in your repo copies)

### `Scope_header_v2.py` (both paths)

- **Default coupling is AC again** (audio-style). Use **`PTS3_SCOPE_COUPLING=DC`** if you want DC.
- **Coupling / trigger / channel select** are sent only on the **first** `configure()` for that `Oscilloscope` instance. Later calls (e.g. each step in a sweep) only update **scales + horizontal + `ACQ:STATE RUN`**, so we don’t hammer the instrument.
- **`*OPC?` is off by default** (it can destabilize some VISA stacks). Set **`PTS3_SCOPE_OPC=1`** only if you need it.
- **`*CLS`** only on the first full setup (unless **`PTS3_SCOPE_CLS=1`**).

### `AUTO_PTS3v17.py` (both copies)

- **`_scope_usb_release_delay()`** after every `with Oscilloscope(...)` block (GUI + CLI, mode + sweep).  
  Default pause: **0.35 s** after the scope is closed, before the rest of the job finishes (so the **next** subprocess is less likely to reopen USB too soon).  
  Override with **`PTS3_VISA_USB_RELEASE_SEC`** (set to **`0`** to disable).

---

## What you should do on the bench

1. **Copy** the updated `Scope_header_v2.py` and `AUTO_PTS3v17.py` into **`d:\PTS3_Modified\PTS3_Modified\`** (same as in your log).
2. **Strongly prefer Python 3.12** for the connector / CLI if you can (3.13 + VISA is a known pain). Point **`PTS3_PYTHON_PATH`** to 3.12 if ERP uses a launcher.
3. Set **`PTS3_VISA_RESOURCE`** to your exact `USB0::...::INSTR` string so we **avoid** extra `list_resources()` when possible.
4. If it still crashes, increase the pause:  
   `set PTS3_VISA_USB_RELEASE_SEC=0.6`

After this, Mode 3 / 2 should run in **new subprocesses** without the previous process dying on the way out, and the scope should stay on **AC** unless you set **`PTS3_SCOPE_COUPLING=DC`**.

The **`SyntaxError: Unexpected token ')'`** comes from a **missing closing brace** on `hide_operator_fields`.

## What went wrong

After this block:

```javascript
    if (frm.fields_dict.lanes) {
      frm.set_df_property("lanes", "hidden", 1);
    }

  function ensure_lane1(frm) {
```

there must be a **`}`** that **ends** `hide_operator_fields`. In your paste that **`}` is missing**, so JavaScript thinks `ensure_lane1` and everything after it are still inside `hide_operator_fields`. When the parser reaches the final `})();`, the brackets no longer match and you get **Unexpected token ')'**.

## Fix (one line)

Insert **`}`** immediately before `function ensure_lane1`:

```javascript
    if (frm.fields_dict.lanes) {
      frm.set_df_property("lanes", "hidden", 1);
    }
  }

  function ensure_lane1(frm) {
```

So the corrected block is:

```javascript
  function hide_operator_fields(frm) {
    var hidden = ["naming_series", "name_serial_slug", "name_op_short", "test_status", "station_name", "operator", "remarks"];
    hidden.forEach(function (fn) {
      if (frm.fields_dict[fn]) {
        frm.set_df_property(fn, "hidden", 1);
      }
    });
    if (frm.fields_dict.target_pc) {
      frm.set_df_property("target_pc", "hidden", 0);
      frm.set_df_property("target_pc", "read_only", 0);
    }
    if (frm.fields_dict.lanes) {
      frm.set_df_property("lanes", "hidden", 1);
    }
  }

  function ensure_lane1(frm) {
```

Here’s what was going wrong and what we changed.

### Cause

We used **`frm._pcb_pts_jump_installed`** so the buttons were only added **once** per form instance. On every **`refresh`**, Frappe **clears** the custom toolbar and then runs your client script again. Because the flag stayed set, the script **returned early** and **never re-added** the buttons—until a **full reload** gave you a new form object (flag reset).

That matches “works only after hard refresh.”

### Fix

1. **Removed that guard** everywhere so **PTS1** / **PTS3** actions are registered on **every** `refresh` (normal navigation, save, reload, etc.).

2. **Duplicate scripts**: With both **Visual Timeline Display** and **PCB Ledger Open PTS1 and PTS3** enabled, you’d get **four** identical actions. **`UPSERT_PCB_LEDGER_VISUAL_TIMELINE_DISPLAY_RIGHT_COLUMN.py`** now **turns off** the standalone **“PCB Ledger Open PTS1 and PTS3”** script after it deploys the timeline script (buttons stay only in the timeline client script).

Installers were run on your Docker site: timeline updated, duplicate script **disabled**.

### What you should do

- One normal refresh on **PCB Ledger** should be enough now (hard refresh not required for this bug).
- On **other servers**, redeploy with **`UPSERT_PCB_LEDGER_VISUAL_TIMELINE_DISPLAY_RIGHT_COLUMN.py`** (or copy the JS change) and run **`INSTALL`** only if you don’t use the timeline script.

**Note:** If you run **`INSTALL_PCB_LEDGER_PTS1_PTS3_JUMP_BUTTONS.py`** again **without** running the UPSERT after it, the duplicate script will be turned **on** again. Run the UPSERT after INSTALL, or leave the duplicate disabled under **Customize → Client Script**.

Here’s what was going wrong and what we changed.

## 1. **Scope readings were 0 in software (ERP log)**

The Tek driver was sending **`*CLS`** on **every** `configure_for_frequency()` (once per sweep step). On many TBS scopes that **clears measurement state**, so **`MEASUrement:IMMed:VALue?`** often stays **0.0** until things settle—while the **screen** can still look fine.

**Updates in `Scope_header_v2.py` (both copies):**

- **`*CLS`** only if you set **`PTS3_SCOPE_CLS=1`** (off by default).
- **Default coupling** is **`DC`** (override with **`PTS3_SCOPE_COUPLING=AC`** if you need AC).
- After scale/trigger setup, **`*OPC?`** so the instrument finishes before measuring.
- **`_measure`**: short delay after setting type, then **a second read** if the first value is 0.

Together, that should align **SCPI numbers** with what you see on the scope.

---

## 2. **ERP looked “empty” / no Excel / sweep from connector**

For **`step_sweep`**, the connector **used the runner daemon** by default. The daemon:

- Does **not** write the **`PCB_READINGS\…xlsx`** file the CLI writes.
- Sends **`artifact_paths`** as empty → **PTS3 Result** shows **no Excel / artifacts**.
- Still had the same **`read_all`** path (zeros made tables all **0.00**).

**Update in `pts3_connector.py` (both copies):**

- **`step_sweep`** now uses **`AUTO_PTS3v17.py --cli` in a subprocess** by default (same as your standalone test): **Excel + `artifact_paths`** go to ERP like the GUI/CLI.
- To use the **daemon** for sweep again (hot scope, no Excel from worker):  
  **`PTS3_USE_RUNNER_FOR_SWEEP=1`**

### AI  ``

Here’s what was wrong and what we changed.

### Root causes
1. **`save_final_result` could fail silently** – The connector always treated the HTTP call as success. Frappe still returns **200** with `{"ok": false, "reason": "..."}` when the server script rejects the payload, so the run looked “done” while **no row was written** (or you only saw partial metadata from other paths).
2. **Partial payloads** – Sometimes the sweep **`graph`** had `freqs` / arrays but **`left_right_diff_summary`** had empty `left` / `right` / `diff` maps, so the DB stored empty summary/chart-related data.
3. **Desk JSON fields** – `safe_json` / `book_safe_json` only handled **strings**. If the form ever gives an **already-parsed object**, the UI treated it as empty and showed “No sweep data” / blank mode.

### What we implemented

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| **`pts3_connector.py`** | `api_save_final_result` uses `call_pts3_api_json`, checks `ok`, **raises** with the ERP `reason` if save fails (timeout 120s). On `completed`, **merges** accumulated `mode_values` and fills an empty **`graph`** for single-mode runs when needed. |
| **`pts3_api_server_script.py`** | If a **sweep** `graph` has data but L/R/D maps are empty, **builds** `left_right_diff_summary` from `freqs` + arrays. If **`mode_values`** has one mode but **`graph`** is empty, **sets** a proper mode `graph` before insert. |
| **`pts3_result_client_script.js`** | **`safe_json`** accepts both JSON **strings** and **objects**. |
| **`pts3_book.js`** | Same for **`book_safe_json`**. |

### What you should do next
1. **Redeploy the server script** on the site (same process you use for `pts3_api`, e.g. `INSTALL_PTS3_BOOK_AND_API_VIA_AUTO_EXECUTOR.py` or your Frappe console installer) so **`pts3_api_server_script.py`** changes go live.
2. **Redeploy client scripts** for **PTS3 Result** and **PTS3 Book** if those are not loaded from this repo automatically.

### AI  ``

Here’s what was going wrong and what we changed.

### What was happening
Pressing **Step sweep** / **Mode** in ERP starts a **new** `AUTO_PTS3v17.py` process when **`pts3_runner_daemon` isn’t used**. Every run then pays the full cost: Python start, imports (Sheets, Tk, etc.), PyVISA discovery, and opening the scope — then it can play tones and read the scope. That matches your log.

### What we want
Keep **one long-lived process** that holds the **VISA session**, and have the **connector** open the scope **before** operators rely on it:

1. **`pts3_runner_daemon.py`**  
   - New commands: `init`, `scope_init`, `warm`, `warmup`  
   - They only call `ScopeSession.ensure_connected(...)` and emit  
     `{"type":"init_complete","ok":true,"resource":"..."}`  
   - The scope stays open in that process for later `step_sweep` / `mode*`.

2. **`pts3_connector.py`**  
   - On startup (before the poll loop): **`prepare_scope_for_station()`**  
     - Optionally **`PTS3_AUTO_START_RUNNER=1`**: starts `pts3_runner_daemon.py` if nothing is listening on the port.  
     - Sends **`{"cmd":"init"}`** to the runner (with retries so auto-start can finish).  
   - When a job runs, it still **prefers the runner** so you don’t spawn a cold `AUTO_PTS3v17` each time.

### What you should do on the test PC
1. **Recommended:** Run the daemon when the PC logs in (Task Scheduler shortcut or batch), **or** set:
   - `PTS3_AUTO_START_RUNNER=1`  
   so the connector starts the daemon for you.
2. Restart the **connector** and confirm logs like:
   - `[PTS3] Oscilloscope pre-initialized (runner): USB0::...`
   - On a job: `[PTS3] Using runner 127.0.0.1:8765 (scope session kept hot)`
3. If you still see **`START AUTO_PTS3v17.py`** and **Google Sheets** on each job, the runner isn’t reachable — fix port/firewall or path to `pts3_runner_daemon.py`.

**Note:** `AUTO_PTS3v17.py` is only “instant” for music + reads when jobs go through the **runner**. A subprocess run will always re-initialize VISA for that process; the runner is what makes the scope **ready before** and **between** button presses.

### AI  ``

Yes. That block is driven by **one DocType field** that holds **JSON as text**, and the “Metadata” line is **part of that same JSON**, not a second field.

### What you’re looking at

- **Stored on the document:** the field **`left_right_diff_summary_json`** on **PTS3 Result** (type is usually **Code** or **Long Text**, storing a JSON string).
- **Parsed shape:** something like:
  - `metadata` → e.g. `{"serial":"a123"}` → the UI prints it as **Metadata: …**
  - `left` / `right` / `diff` → objects keyed by frequency (e.g. `40hz`, `42hz`, …) → the **Left / Right / Diff** table

Your **PTS3 Result** client script does exactly that: it parses `left_right_diff_summary_json`, reads `t.metadata`, and stringifies it for the “Metadata” line; the table uses `t.left`, `t.right`, `t.diff`.

```363:377:c:\Users\pc\Desktop\PCB_IQC_ERPNext_Project\EXAMPLES\CHARGPT  TRIAL\PTS3 test\pts3_result_client_script.js
  function render_lrd_summary(frm) {
    var t = safe_json(frm.doc.left_right_diff_summary_json, null);
    if (!t || typeof t !== "object") {
      return '<div class="pts3-result-section"><h4>Left / Right / Diff Summary</h4><p class="pts3-result-no-data">No data</p></div>';
    }
    var meta = t.metadata || {};
    var left = t.left || {};
    var right = t.right || {};
    var diff = t.diff || {};
    // ...
    if (Object.keys(meta).length) {
      html += "<p><strong>Metadata:</strong> " + escape_html(JSON.stringify(meta)) + "</p>";
    }
```

So: **`{"serial":"a123"}`** is **`metadata` inside `left_right_diff_summary_json`**. The canonical PCB serial for the result is still normally **`pcb_serial_no`** on the DocType; `metadata.serial` is extra data whoever builds the JSON chose to embed there.

Here’s what was going wrong and what we changed.

### Cause
The **PTS3 Test** screen shows charts from **lane** fields (`live_graph_json` / `live_table_json`), which the connector updates during the run. The **PTS3 Result** row is filled only from the **`save_final_result`** payload. In your case that payload often arrived **without** nested `graph` / `left_right_diff_summary` (Frappe/REST can mangle or drop deep `dict` fields on `result`), so the doc kept **Pass / Max / run_id** but stored **empty** `final_graph_json` and `left_right_diff_summary_json`.

### Fix (implemented)

1. **Connector** (`pts3_connector.py`)  
   - Sends a parallel **`result_json`** string: `json.dumps(result, default=str)`  
   - Server fills any missing `graph`, `left_right_diff_summary`, `table`, `mode_values`, `raw_result` from that string when the `result` dict is incomplete.

2. **Server script** (`pts3_api_server_script.py`)  
   - Parses **`result_json`** and merges into `result_in` before `to_dict`.  
   - **If those are still empty**, reads **`live_graph_json`** and **`live_table_json`** from **lane 1** (same run) and uses them to set `r["graph"]` and `r["left_right_diff_summary"]` before inserting **PTS3 Result**.

So even when the HTTP `result` object is stripped, the server can still recover the same sweep data that powers the Test page.

### What you need to do
1. **Redeploy** the updated **`pts3_api_server_script.py`** on the site (replace the `pts3_api` Server Script).  
2. **Restart** the station **connector** so it sends **`result_json`**.  
3. Run a **new** step sweep and open **PTS3 Result** — graphs and L/R/D should persist.

**Already saved** results that were written with empty JSON will **not** auto-fix; only **new** completions get the fix. If you need old rows repaired, say so and we can add a small backfill from `live_*` or Excel.

In your PTS3 script the **vertical “candles”** (the three columns per mode: Left / Right / Difference) get their **horizontal width** from layout math, then from one knob you already have.

### Main knob: `candleWidthScale` (in `MODE_HBAR`)

```97:98:c:\Users\pc\Desktop\PCB_IQC_ERPNext_Project\EXAMPLES\CHARGPT  TRIAL\PTS3 test\pts3_result_client_script.js
    /** Multiplier on bar width after layout (then clamped to fit the group slot). */
    candleWidthScale: 1,
```

- **`1`** = default width.  
- **`1.2`**–**`1.4`** = noticeably **wider** candles (until they hit the clamp).  
- **`0.7`**–**`0.85`** = **thinner** candles.

Width is still **capped** so the three bars + gaps stay inside each mode’s column (see the `clusterW > groupSlotW` block around lines 893–897).

### Other things that change candle width indirectly

| Setting | Effect |
|--------|--------|
| **`plotWidth`** | Larger → more horizontal space per mode group → wider possible candles. |
| **`candleGroupGap`** | **Smaller** → more width left for each group → candles can be wider. |
| **`candleInnerGap`** (or **`innerGap`** if `candleInnerGap` is `null`) | **Smaller** gap between the three bars → each bar can be **wider** for the same group width. |

So: for “wider candles” without touching layout much, raise **`candleWidthScale`** first; if it doesn’t grow enough, **lower `candleGroupGap`** or **increase `plotWidth`**, or **lower `candleInnerGap` / `innerGap`**.

### Part 1 – Backend API (`pts3_book_api`)

#### 1.1. Whitelisted API method

Create a small Python module in your PTS3 app, e.g.  
`pts3/pts3/doctype/pts3_result/pts3_book_api.py`:

```python
import frappe

@frappe.whitelist()
def get_pts3_book(pcb_serial_no: str, limit: int = 20, offset: int = 0):
    """Return grouped history for one PCB serial.

    Input:
      pcb_serial_no (str)
      limit (int)
      offset (int)

    Output:
      {
        "pcb_serial_no": "...",
        "run_count": int,
        "latest_run": {...} or None,
        "runs": [ {...}, ... ]
      }
    """
    pcb_serial_no = (pcb_serial_no or "").strip()
    if not pcb_serial_no:
        return {
            "pcb_serial_no": "",
            "run_count": 0,
            "latest_run": None,
            "runs": []
        }

    # Count
    run_count = frappe.db.count(
        "PTS3 Result",
        filters={"pcb_serial_no": pcb_serial_no}
    )

    if not run_count:
        return {
            "pcb_serial_no": pcb_serial_no,
            "run_count": 0,
            "latest_run": None,
            "runs": []
        }

    # Newest first
    fields = [
        "name",
        "datetime",
        "operation",
        "pass_fail",
        "dominant_channel",
        "max_value",
        "run_id",
    ]

    runs = frappe.get_all(
        "PTS3 Result",
        filters={"pcb_serial_no": pcb_serial_no},
        fields=fields,
        order_by="datetime desc, creation desc",
        limit_start=int(offset or 0),
        limit_page_length=int(limit or 20),
    )

    # Latest run = first row from same ordering, independent of pagination
    latest = frappe.get_all(
        "PTS3 Result",
        filters={"pcb_serial_no": pcb_serial_no},
        fields=fields,
        order_by="datetime desc, creation desc",
        limit_start=0,
        limit_page_length=1,
    )
    latest_run = latest[0] if latest else None

    return {
        "pcb_serial_no": pcb_serial_no,
        "run_count": run_count,
        "latest_run": latest_run,
        "runs": runs,
    }
```

Then expose it in `hooks.py` (if you prefer REST style):

### Why it was happening
Your `PTS3 Test` page shows data because it reads **lane live fields** (`live_graph_json` / `live_table_json`) while the run is happening.

But the `PTS3 Result` doc was being saved from `save_final_result(result=...)`, and in some cases Frappe was turning nested dicts inside `result` into **stringified Python dicts** (single quotes). ### What I changed (server-side)
In `pts3_api_server_script.py` → `save_final_result`:

- If `result_json` is provided (connector sends it), we now **prefer it as the source of truth** and only fill missing keys from `result`.
- This guarantees we save **real JSON** (not Python dict strings).

### AI  ``

Here’s what was implemented and how it maps to your desired pattern.

### Format

**`{pcb_serial_slug}_{short_action}_{series}`**

- **Serial**: taken from lane 1 `pcb_serial_no`, slugified (letters/digits, other chars → `_`, max 60 chars). Empty → `UNKNOWN`.
- **Sweep vs mode**: `step_sweep` → `sweep`, `full_test` → `full`, `mode1` / `mode2` / … stay as-is.
- **Series**: Frappe’s `{#####}` counter (same idea as the old numeric tail).

Example names: `acvc_sweep_00001`, `SN12345_mode1_00002`.

Slashes are **not** used in the **name** (they’re awkward in URLs and links). You still get a clear **sweep vs mode** segment.

### Repo changes

1. **`create_pts3_doctypes_v1.py`**  
   - New **PTS3 Test** installs use  
     `autoname = "format:{name_serial_slug}_{name_op_short}_{#####}"`  
     and **`naming_rule = "Expression"`**, with hidden fields **`name_serial_slug`** and **`name_op_short`.**

Here’s what was going wrong and what we changed.

### 1. **PyVISA “access violation”**
NI‑VISA + **Python 3.13** + Tek USB is touchy. You were calling **`list_resources()` twice** before opening the scope:

1. At **import** in `AUTO_PTS3v17.py` (old code).
2. Again inside **`Scope_header_v2.Oscilloscope.__init__`** every time you created a scope.

That second enumeration often triggered the fault you saw in `_find_resources` / `open`.

**Changes:**
- **`AUTO_PTS3v17.py`**: No VISA scan at import. Added **`ensure_visa()`**, which creates one `ResourceManager`, runs **`list_resources()` once**, and sets `scope_res`. GUI/CLI call **`ensure_visa()`** before any scope use.
- **`Scope_header_v2.py`**: If **`rm`** and **`resource_name`** are both passed (normal PTS3 path), it **opens that resource only** and **does not** call **`list_resources()`** again.

Optional: set **`PTS3_VISA_RESOURCE=USB0::0x0699::0x03C4::C012223::INSTR`** (your address) so `ensure_visa()` **skips** `list_resources()` completely.

### 2. **“Playing: 0 Hz” in ERP**
Mode runs didn’t send a **`freq`** field on status events, so the dashboard kept **0 Hz** (sweep is the only path that used to set frequency).

**Change:** During mode capture, the CLI now emits status with **`"freq": 80`** while the 80 Hz tone is active, and **`"freq": 0`** when it stops, so the connector can push **`live_current_freq`** correctly.

### 3. **What you should deploy**
Copy the updated files to **`d:\PTS3_Modified\PTS3_Modified\`** (or your live folder):

- `AUTO_PTS3v17.py`
- `Scope_header_v2.py`

### 4. **If crashes continue**
- Prefer **Python 3.12.x** for PyVISA/NI‑VISA on Windows until stacks catch up with 3.13.  
- Install the latest **NI‑VISA** runtime and Tek **USB** driver.  
- Only one app should own the scope at a time (close Tek OpenChoice, etc.).

Your log still showed a valid **Mode0** line after the faults, so the hardware path works; reducing duplicate VISA calls should remove most of those fatal exceptions.

### AI  ``

Summary of the layout and size controls:

### **Step Sweep**

```javascript
SWEEP_CHART = {
  // ... existing options ...
  width: null,        // Chart width in px (null = use CHART.width)
  height: null,       // Chart height in px (null = use CHART.height)
  layout: "chartTop", // "chartTop" | "chartLeft" | "chartRight"
  tableWidth: null,   // e.g. "200px", "25%"
  chartWidth: null    // e.g. "400px", "500px"
};
```

- **layout**
  - `"chartTop"` – chart above, table below
  - `"chartLeft"` – chart left, table right
  - `"chartRight"` – table left, chart right

### **Mode**

```javascript
MODE_CHART = {
  // ... existing options ...
  width: null,         // Chart width in px (null = use CHART.width)
  height: null,        // Chart height in px (null = use CHART.height)
  layout: "tableLeft", // "tableLeft" | "tableRight"
  tableWidth: "180px", // e.g. "180px", "25%"
  chartWidth: null     // e.g. "350px" (null = flex:1)
};
```

- **layout**
  - `"tableLeft"` – table left, chart right
  - `"tableRight"` – chart left, table right

### **Chart size**

```javascript
CHART = {
  width: 1000,   // Default chart width (px)
  height: 500    // Default chart height (px)
};
```

Override per chart:

- `SWEEP_CHART.width`, `SWEEP_CHART.height`
- `MODE_CHART.width`, `MODE_CHART.height`

### **Table size**

```javascript
TABLE_STYLE = {
  fontSize: "0.85em"   // e.g. "0.85em", "12px", "1rem"
};
```

### **Examples**

| Goal | Change |
|------|--------|
| Step Sweep side by side | `SWEEP_CHART.layout: "chartLeft"` or `"chartRight"` |
| Mode chart on left | `MODE_CHART.layout: "tableRight"` |
| Mode table wider | `MODE_CHART.tableWidth: "250px"` |
| Mode chart taller | `MODE_CHART.height: 300` |
| Smaller table text | `TABLE_STYLE.fontSize: "0.75em"` |

**Almost** — the file is *very close*, but there’s **one critical bug** in your current `pts3_api_server_script.py` that will break the `save_final_result` flow.

### What’s good
- **Run ID format**: ✅ `pts3_alloc_session_run_id()` generates `pts3run_<serial>_<testdoc>_<series>` (confirmed).
- **Keeps sweep plot when running modes**: ✅ `request_lane_action` uses `keep_live` to avoid clearing `live_graph_json/live_table_json` for mode steps (confirmed).
- **Upsert model**: ✅ It’s intended to upsert by `run_id` and merge sweep/mode (confirmed).
- **Version flag**: ✅ `get_status_snapshot` returns `api_version` so you can verify deployment (confirmed).

### The critical issue (must fix)
In `save_final_result`, your code has this structure:

```python
try:
   ...
except Exception:
    pass
    operation = ...
    dt_str = ...
    ...
```

Because `operation/dt_str/...` are **indented under the `except`**, they run **only when an exception happens**.  
If no exception happens (normal case), `operation` never gets set and the rest of the save logic won’t run correctly.

You can see this in the snippet around:

- `except Exception:`
- `pass`
- then `operation = (r.get("operation") or "").strip()` is still inside that `except`

### Fix
Move these lines **out of the `except` block** (dedent them to the same level as the `try:`):

- `operation = ...`
- `dt_str = ...`
- `table = ...`
- `graph = ...`
- `mode_values = ...`
- and everything that follows in the “validate + insert/update” part

### After you fix it
- Mode1 → Mode2 won’t trigger duplicate run_id anymore.
- Mode2 won’t erase sweep plot (already handled).
- Results will merge into the same PTS3 Result row.

If you want, I can patch that indentation bug for you right now in `pts3_api_server_script.py` (and the nested copy too) — it’s a surgical fix.

### AI  ``

### 1. “Four lanes” UI

- That dark screenshot with **Lane 1..4** is from the older **multi‑lane script** (`pts3_client_script.js`).
- Your ERP single‑lane operator flow uses lane **1 only**; lanes **2–4** are just empty shells and don’t affect the bench.
- We’ll keep designing everything around **one lane** (lane 1). You can ignore lanes 2–4 in that view.

---

### 2. How `raw_result_json` works today

Right now, each ERP job creates **one PTS3 Result per operation**:

- **Step Sweep** result:
  - `operation = "step_sweep"`
  - `raw_result_json` contains only:

    ```json
    { "sweep_averages": [ [40, p1, p2, diff], ... ] }
    ```

- **Mode X** result:
  - `operation = "mode1"` (or 2/3/0)
  - `raw_result_json` contains only one mode snippet, e.g.:

    ```json
    {
      "mode": 1,
      "avg_p1": ...,
      "avg_p2": ...,
      "avg_diff": ...,
      "stimulus_80hz_loop": true
    }
    ```

So when you open the **step_sweep** result you see only sweep; when you open the **mode1** result you see only the mode numbers.

---

### 3. What you want

For each **run** (same run_id), you want **one combined raw JSON** that looks conceptually like:

```json
{
  "sweep_averages": [ ... ],
  "mode0_result": { "avg_p1": ..., "avg_p2": ..., "avg_diff": ... },
  "mode1_result": { "avg_p1": ..., "avg_p2": ..., "avg_diff": ... },
  "mode2_result": { "avg_p1": ..., "avg_p2": ..., "avg_diff": ... },
  "mode3_result": { "avg_p1": ..., "avg_p2": ..., "avg_diff": ... }
}
```

So:

- **Press Step Sweep** → fills `sweep_averages`.
- **Press Mode 0** → adds/updates `mode0_result`.
- **Press Mode 1** → adds/updates `mode1_result`.
- etc., all **for the same run_id**.

---

### 4. Where this must change

To get that behavior, we need to change **only the ERP server script**, not the bench scripts:

- File: `PTS3 test/pts3_api_server_script.py`
- Inside the `api_cmd == "save_final_result"` block, around:

```python
raw_result = r.get("raw_result") or {}
rr_str = (payload.get("pre_raw_result_json") or "").strip() or to_json_str(raw_result)
```

The idea is:

1. **Look up existing result for this run_id / lane / PTS3 Test** (if any) and parse its `raw_result_json` into a dict, say `combined`.
2. Treat the incoming `raw_result` as a **snippet**:
   - If it has `sweep_averages`, set `combined["sweep_averages"] = raw_result["sweep_averages"]`.
   - If it has `mode` 0/1/2/3 and `avg_p1/avg_p2/avg_diff`, set:

     ```python
     combined[f"mode{mode}_result"] = {
         "avg_p1": raw_result.get("avg_p1"),
         "avg_p2": raw_result.get("avg_p2"),
         "avg_diff": raw_result.get("avg_diff"),
         "stimulus_80hz_loop": raw_result.get("stimulus_80hz_loop"),
     }
     ```

3. Store `combined` back as the new `raw_result_json` string (`rr_str = to_json_str(combined)`).

Effect:

- First time (Step Sweep) → JSON has just `sweep_averages`.
- After Mode1 for same run_id → JSON includes both `sweep_averages` **and** `mode1_result`.
- After Mode0/2/3 → JSON grows more keys, but all in **one** raw blob.

We can implement this merge logic in `pts3_api_server_script.py` next if you want; it will only take a small helper function plus replacing the `rr_str` line.

### AI  ``

Here is what was wrong in **`AUTO_PTS3v17.py`** alone and what we changed.

### Problems
1. **`PTS3_VISA_RESOURCE.txt`** was only read **next to the script**. If the file lived elsewhere or you fixed it after a failed run, behavior was confusing.
2. **`_visa_initialized`** was set **before** a successful `scope_res`, so a failed first `ensure_visa()` could **block later success** (no retry after adding the file).
3. On **Python 3.13** there was **no** escape hatch except setting the resource manually (enumeration is intentionally off).

### Fixes (all in `AUTO_PTS3v17.py`)

1. **`_visa_txt_search_dirs()`** — loads `PTS3_VISA_RESOURCE.txt` from the **first** path that exists, in order:
   - folder of **`AUTO_PTS3v17.py`** (same as before)
   - `cwd` if different
   - **`%LOCALAPPDATA%\PTS3\`**
   - **`%USERPROFILE%\.pts3\`**

2. **`ensure_visa()`** — **`_visa_initialized`** is only set when **`scope_res`** is successfully set; failed 3.13 path **does not** lock out a later call after you add a txt file or env var.

3. **`PTS3_VISA_ALLOW_ENUM=1`** — optional, **unsafe** on 3.13: runs `list_resources()` with a warning (for machines where it does not crash).

4. **CLI `--visa-resource "USB0::..."`** — sets `PTS3_VISA_RESOURCE` before any work, so you can run standalone without a txt file, e.g.  
   `python AUTO_PTS3v17.py --cli --mode mode0 --serial TEST --visa-resource "USB0::..."`

### What you still need for a real scope on 3.13
Either:
- **One line** in **`PTS3_VISA_RESOURCE.txt`** in one of the folders above, or  
- **`setx PTS3_VISA_RESOURCE "USB0::..."`**, or  
- **`--visa-resource`** on the command line, or  
- **`PTS3_VISA_ALLOW_ENUM=1`** only if you accept possible crashes.

The VISA string should match your scope (e.g. from **NI MAX** or `py -3.12 discover_pts3_visa.py`).

The **Station** field is the identifier of the PC that runs the PTS3 connector (the test station).

**What to enter**

- The **hostname** of the connector PC, e.g.:
  - `PTS3-PC-01` (as in the placeholder)

**How to find the hostname**

- **Windows:** `echo %COMPUTERNAME%` in Command Prompt, or `hostname` in PowerShell.
- **Linux:** `hostname` in a terminal.

## Recommended architecture (cleanest + scalable)

**Build a new Desk Page / Workspace page: `PTS3 Book`** that **queries existing `PTS3 Result` records grouped by `pcb_serial_no`** (no storage/model changes).  
This is the cleanest because it **doesn’t duplicate data**, scales well, and keeps **`PTS3 Result` unchanged**.

Why not a new DocType?
- A `PTS3 PCB Book` DocType would mostly be a **redundant “index table”** (since runs already exist). It adds sync/maintenance problems unless you truly need manual notes/workflow per PCB.

Why not only a Query Report?
- Query Reports are great for **lists**, but a “book” UI (summary + expandable run history + quick open buttons) is usually smoother as a **custom Page**.

---

## What to implement

### Option A (recommended): New Desk Page `PTS3 Book`
- **Frontend**: a Frappe Desk Page with:
  - Search box for `pcb_serial_no`
  - “Book header” summary
  - Run list (newest first) with “Open Result” buttons
- **Backend**: a whitelisted server method (or Server Script API) that returns:
  - summary for that `pcb_serial_no`
  - list of matching `PTS3 Result` docs (paged)

**Key DB requirement (for speed):**
- Ensure `PTS3 Result.pcb_serial_no` is **indexed** (or set as “Search Index” + DB index). This makes large histories fast.

### Option B: Query Report “PTS3 Book (Grouped)”
- Report grouped by `pcb_serial_no`, with run count + latest run fields.
- Clicking a row opens a filtered list or the latest `PTS3 Result`.
- Faster to build, but less “book-like” UX.

### Option C: New DocType `PTS3 PCB Book` (only if you need per-PCB notes/workflow)
- Stores **one row per PCB**, and links to results.
- Still does **not** merge runs; it’s just a container + optional notes/status.

---

## If you choose **Option A**: required changes

### Backend (API)
Add an API method like:
- **Input**: `pcb_serial_no`, `limit`, `offset`
- **Output**:
  - **pcb_serial_no**
  - **run_count**
  - **latest_run**: `{name, datetime, operation, pass_fail, dominant_channel, max_value, run_id}`
  - **runs[]** newest first: list of `{name, datetime, operation, pass_fail, dominant_channel, max_value, run_id}`

### Frontend (Page UI)
**Book page layout (single PCB)**

- **Header**
  - PCB Serial No: `XYZ`
  - Total runs: `N`
  - Latest run summary (Pass/Fail, Dominant, Max, Datetime, Operation)
  - Button: **Open Latest Result**
- **Run History (newest first)**
  - Table rows:
    - Datetime | Operation | Pass/Fail | Dominant | Max | Run ID | **Open**
  - Pagination (“Load more”)

---

## If you choose **Option C** (new DocType): exact fields

DocType: **`PTS3 PCB Book`**
- **pcb_serial_no** (Data, **Unique**, required, indexed)
- **latest_result** (Link → `PTS3 Result`, read-only)
- **latest_datetime** (Datetime, read-only)
- **run_count** (Int, read-only)
- **latest_pass_fail** (Select, read-only)
- **latest_dominant_channel** (Data/Select, read-only)
- **latest_max_value** (Float, read-only)
- **notes** (Small Text / Text Editor, optional)
- (Optional) **status** (Select: Active/Hold/etc.)

The “runs list” should still be **queried from `PTS3 Result`**, not stored.

---

## Summary recommendation
- **Best overall**: **New Desk Page `PTS3 Book` + API query** (no new DocType), with an **index on `PTS3 Result.pcb_serial_no`**.
- Keeps your **one-run-per-record** model untouched and makes history readable for heavy-run PCBs.
